There was still work to be done, so he joined the others in assisting with the looting and hauling of the Hunters and other units.
Not far from the shelter, they had created what resembled a graveyard... or perhaps more accurately, a junkyard.
It was where they piled the A.I.
Soldiers and units that were too heavily damaged or too difficult to dismantle for spare parts.
Their fate would most likely to be melted in a furnace.
Their metals could be converted into barricades, formed to forge traps, or repurposed for defensive structures.
As for those with intact components, they were carefully carried to the warehouse.
Survivors worked tirelessly as they stripped plating and salvaged the cores inside.
Soon, even the traps were reset, and the barricades were reinforced with fresh layers of steel.
By the time the last body of Hound was dragged into place, darkness had already fallen.
And of course, the generators were already on, giving light within the building.
"Good work, everyone!
We can all finally rest..." Kai said.
Everyone cheered as they returned to their quarters to rest.
Meanwhile, Kai and the others could now focus on the items they had obtained.
"Let’s see..." Kai muttered as he checked his inventory.
His attention fell on the Gene Weapon.
As expected, it was still in cube form with restrained energy.
He held it in his palm, and it was truly heavy, comparable to the low-grade Gene Weapons.
The cube just looked normal, but it was cold to the touch...
"So this is the Specter Edge..." he muttered.
He could not sense the dormant power within, but he knew that it was the real deal when he got the notification.
[ You have obtained a Dormant Gene Weapon. ]
[ Do you wish to awaken it and become its owner? ]
There was only one answer.
"Yes." Kai answered.
[ Activating Gene Weapon - Specter Edge ]
[ Connection in progress... ]
[ Synchronizing Spirit Resonance... ]
[ Warning: Gene Weapon requires a compatible Spirit Flow. ]
[ Compatibility Check: Passed. ]
[ Awakening Sequence Initiated. ]
A low hum filled the air as gears inside the cube began to shift.
Kai’s grip tightened, and the panels unfolded slowly...
Soon, thin lines of light spilled out...
The cube then elongated, reshaping itself into a weapon.
Slowly, its true form emerged... a dagger that was lustrous and black!
[ Gene Weapon Awakened: Specter Edge ]
[ Grade: Mid ]
[ Type: Spirit‐Infused Dagger ]
[ Effects: +15% Armor Penetration against mechanical units.
Signal Disruption: Attacks have a chance to disable enemy sensors. ]
[ Hidden Attribute: ??? (Requires further appraisal) ]
Hu~
Kai exhaled.
He felt really excited now.
At first glance, it looked like any ordinary dagger, but the System’s notifications told him otherwise.
This was no simple blade... it was a weapon designed to cut through armor and disrupt the A.I.’s signal nodes.
He raised it, feeling the weight settle naturally in his hand.
"This... this is perfect," Kai muttered...
"Not flashy, but deadly.
Exactly what we need."
Now, he couldn’t help but recall Angelo’s shelter.
’I guess it’s time to make a visit..’

chapters.title: Chapter 213: Angelo’s Shelter and the Transformation
paragraphs: Meanwhile, the swamp village, what Angelo and his men now called Haven‐28, had been eerily quiet after the Global Event. The fog had thickened over the settlement, protecting them from outside interference, but it didn’t matter right now...
Angelo stood at the edge of their makeshift graveyard, staring at the rows of markers jutting from the mud.

Seventeen of his people had fallen during the seven‐day ordeal. The fog that cloaked their settlement had not been enough to protect them from the unending sweeps of Drones, Hunters, Swarmers, Hounds, and Dominion units.
The graves were simple.
Wooden planks carved from scavenged debris marked some with names, while others were left blank because no one could remember them.
In the chaos of battle, identities had been lost. Angelo sighed as he counted them again...
Seventeen.
A huge chunk of their strength was gone.
During the event, the swamp had slowed the Hounds since their mechanical limbs struggled in the waste.
But the drones and swarmers had no such weakness. They flew above the fog, scanning without issues.
The Dominion units had been the worst. Those alien‐like vessels carrying Bomber Swarmers were terrifying...
Each time they rained destruction from the skies, someone died. Even their traps, sharpened stakes, hidden pits, and crude barricades, had been little more than a delay.
"I need more Serums and Energy Cores..." Angelo muttered as he looked at the salvaged enemy units piled nearby.
Most of them were Hunters.

These units had been terrifying in their own right. With two mechanical tentacles sprouting from their backs, they moved swiftly, climbing walls, leaping barricades, and dragging survivors into the dark.
Angelo still remembered the screams when one of his men was snatched and torn apart before they could intervene.
Yet despite the losses, they had survived thanks to their fuel reserves and the grit of their elite members with special Gene Skills.
"All your sacrifices made us stronger... We will never forget your contribution," Angelo whispered, before he turned back toward the village.
The forty‐two people who remained were hardened survivors now.
Angelo’s "elite" crew had fought tooth and nail, and the System had rewarded them.
They unlocked new Gene Skills... abilities that sharpened reflexes, strengthened endurance, and heightened senses.
Furthermore, they had scavenged better iron plating from fallen Dominion units, reforging them into blades and armor.
And most importantly, they had looted eighteen Plasma Rifles.
The rifles came from an Impulse Ship they had managed to shoot down with their catapult.
It had been sheer luck... Apparently, the ship was transporting weapons elsewhere, and they crippled it enough to salvage the cargo.

Most rifles had five shots left, the lowest only two. None of them possessed the skill to recharge the weapons with Energy Cores, but Angelo wasn’t concerned. The rifles were trump cards, reserved for emergencies. For now, their crossbows, metal bolts, and the catapult would suffice.
"Alright, everyone... back to work!" Angelo ordered before he glanced at the small house with two Survivors in it...
Well, those two consumed Mutagenic Gene Enhancement Serums after the event ended, and apparently, they were undergoing transformation or mutation!
None of them had an idea if they would grow two heads, two pupils, or whatever mutation it was, but they were all looking forward to that...
For now, that had to wait...
Looking around, the settlement was actually small.
Aside from the original buildings and defensive lines, they had patched houses.
Still, the fog concealed their shortcomings from outsiders, so even if their houses weren’t heavily protected, it was fine for now...
"Guys... Do not disturb the two mutating Survivors. Stay clear." Angelo reminded himself as he walked around.
Soon, he met Jasmine, who was handling their food provisions.
Well, food was scarce. They rationed themselves to one meal per day, supplemented by a snack at night... usually dried leaves boiled into bitter tea.
The swamp provided some edible plants, but not enough to sustain them...
A few hours later, inside the largest shack, Angelo’s elite crews gathered.
They were the ones who had fought beside him during the event, the ones who had earned new Gene Skills.
One had developed enhanced vision, able to spot A.I. Units through the fog. Another had gained a skill that hardened his skin against shrapnel.
Angelo himself had unlocked a sharpshooter’s skill, allowing him to fire with high precision.
They sat around a crude table, as they needed to discuss their future...
"We lost too many," one muttered.
"Seventeen... we need to recruit new people. But our food resources must be improved first," another added bitterly.
Angelo nodded. "Food is the key. Without it, we can’t grow stronger. Even with crops planted, it will take months before they’re useful."
The men exchanged glances. They all knew scavenging wasn’t enough anymore. Their plan had to change.
"Sooner or later, we’ll have to loot that place..." Angelo said grimly.
They paused after hearing this... Everyone knew what he meant.
The previous A.I. base that had become a human shelter was the perfect target.
"They have fields of crops," Angelo continued.
"If we take that place, we’ll be set for life. No more rationing scraps, no more bitter tea. Real food and steady supplies."
James, one of his elites, leaned forward. "Then we equip all our Plasma Rifles. If we strike hard and fast, we can overwhelm them."

Angelo nodded... "They survived the event too. They’ll be stronger now, maybe even stronger than us. But they don’t have numbers. They must have suffered losses. If we hit them before they recover, we can win."
The room fell silent. The plan was dangerous, but hunger made men reckless.
Just then, the door burst open. A scout rushed in, breathless.
"We have company!"
The lieutenants stiffened with their hands reaching for weapons.
Angelo rose slowly, as he carried his Plasma Rifle...
"Company?" he repeated.
The scout nodded frantically. "Movement outside the fog. Not machines... humans."
Angelo’s lips curled into a thin smile. "Humans, huh? Then maybe fate has delivered our first opportunity."
Then, at the same time, another messenger came!
Apparently, the two Survivors in the safe house had already completed their mutation, and everyone was shocked by their appearance!

chapters.title: Chapter 215: Building a Shelter
paragraphs: After a couple of days of careful planning, Kai finally confirmed that Haven‐45 was stable and that all injured people were healed...

In any case, the Haven-45 shelter had endured the Global Event without any significant casualties, and the survivors were already rebuilding their defenses and repairing damaged structures, so Kai didn’t really have any concern just yet.
He felt really relieved at that time, knowing that his people were safe. It gave him the confidence to move forward with the next phase.

With preparations complete, Kai gathered his trusted companions. Claire, Ralph, Sera, Althea, and Alfie were all summoned to Freedom Shelter, ready to join him in the raid. Each of them had trained really well...
Claire, Ralph, and Alfie were all Level 20 and above, so their usefulness was obvious.
As for Althea and Sera... They had also improved thanks to the event...
Kai himself stood at the center of the group...
His A‐Grade Sentinel, Atom, stood nearby like a silent guardian.
Mei was at his side with her rifle slung across her shoulder, while looking at the rest of the group.
"Nice lineup... I think this is enough." She muttered as she looked behind.
There were trained workers ready to join them.
They were now equipped with rifles and other weapons that Kai had taken out of his inventory.
"We’re ready!" Noli, the leader of the group, shouted.
Apparently, the ten workers weren’t laborers anymore... they were fighters!
After surviving the global event that lasted for seven days, it wasn’t surprising that Kai included the group.
They were all capable of protecting themselves for now.
Soon, they learned their mission...
The atmosphere was tense but they were resolute to finish this...
Everyone knew the risks of targeting Angelo’s Haven‐28, but they also understood the necessity.
They couldn’t let a hostile group linger around their shelter or they might regret it...

Soon, Kai asked everyone to take out one off-road motorbike for their own transportation... Well, their warehouse has enough of them since he opened a lot of Transport Gift Pack main to obtain the emergency thruster pack, and compact grappling launcher...
Furthermore, he had them wear the protective riding gear included in the pack.
"This is nice..." Mei muttered as this was her first time wearing them.
"They’re a lot more comfortable than I imagined." Sera agreed as she flexed her body...
The protective riding gear from the Transport Gift Packs was more than just clothing, it was survival equipment.
Each set came complete with a reinforced helmet, padded jacket, gloves, pants, and boots. The material was rugged, layered with shock‐absorbing plates and resistant to tearing.
When the group suited up, they immediately felt the difference.
Claire flexed her arms, testing the jacket’s mobility.
"Not bad... I think it adjusted to my physique... Anyway, it’s not too heavy... I can move freely." Ralph said as he knocked his knuckles against the helmet.
"Feels solid..."
Even Alfie, usually quiet, muttered, "This will keep us alive if we crash for sure..."
The workers, too, were satisfied. They never had anything like this before...
Needless to say, the gear gave them confidence, and Kai could see it in their eyes.
Once everyone was equipped, Kai gestured toward the motorbikes. The off‐road machines had sturdy frames built for swamp and mountain terrain.
Each bike came with bulletproof tires, fuel reserves, and compact repair kits. They weren’t flashy, but they were reliable.
Soon, engines were turned on one by one...
The sound echoed through Freedom Shelter’s yard.

Then, the strike force mounted up with helmets secured and rifles strapped to their backs. Atom moved to the front, towering like a sentinel, while Kai revved his own bike and looked back at the group.
"Good job, Noli... Let’s go."
Noli grinned, clutching his digi‐cam. It was thanks to him that they knew where to head.
He had captured photos of the foggy swamp near the mountain... Those images revealed faint outlines of structures hidden in the mist and those pictures had given Kai the coordinates they needed.
The convoy rolled out, engines growling as they sped across uneven terrain.
At first, they were slow because many of them weren’t used to the vehicle just yet.
However, it didn’t take long before it became easy for them...
After a few hours of driving, they noticed fog as they grew closer to the mountain... Then, as they continued, the fog started thickening.
Finally, Kai stopped after seeing the swamp stretched before them...
The convoy then slowed to a halt at the edge of the swamp.
The fog actually clung to the ground, curling even around the roots and reeds, making the visibility poor.
Kai raised his hand, signaling everyone to dismount.
Just like that, engines were cut off one by one, leaving only the eerie silence of the swamp.
Thud...
Boots sank slightly into the damp soil as the strike force spread out with their rifles ready.
"It’s cold here, huh..." Mei muttered as she looked around.
Atom was also there, scanning the mist, while Claire stayed in her position.
Noli then moved ahead, pointing toward a narrow path that wound deeper into the swamp.
"This way," he whispered. "I noticed through the pictures that this path seemed heavily used."
Meanwhile, Kai just smiled as he allowed Noli to lead. He also noticed the path, but he allowed him to take over...
Just like that, the group followed cautiously...
The path was narrow, but it was a way forward.
But just as they began to advance, a sharp sound split the silence.
Bang!
A gunshot echoed through the swamp.
Everyone froze... But Kai immediately sensed something... it carried no killing intent.
From the mist, a voice rang out.
"Why are you here?! We’re no longer accepting trades!"
The strike force exchanged glances. The tone wasn’t hostile enough for an ambush; it sounded more like frustration.
Kai’s lips curled into a faint smile. He understood what was happening.
Angelo’s group had bikes and sold them to many people, like how he had tried to sell them all to him...
And of course, the bikes needed fuel.
Survivors must have been coming here to buy fuel...
Kai then thought of an idea and stepped forward...
"We’re here to look around," he said, lying through his teeth. "I plan to build a shelter here too."

chapters.title: Chapter 216: The Conflict
paragraphs: Mei, Claire, and the rest of the group couldn’t help but pause after hearing Kai’s words. His lie was obvious but they didn’t speak...
’Build a shelter, huh...’Claire wryly smiled as she waited for the other side’s response.
Unexpectedly, the man in the fog lowered his rifle slightly, but his suspicion lingered in his stance.
Soon, however, his voice carried frustration more than hostility.

"Tch... another one. Build a shelter? Dream on. You people keep coming here, thinking you can trade or settle. We told you already! We’re not accepting trades anymore, and this Mist Mountain is ours!"

Kai tilted his head, as he thought of just going with the flow... "Wow... You already claimed this place and you’re not accepting trades? That’s unusual. Survivors need supplies. Fuel, food, weapons... surely you’re still dealing with some fuel? We have a lot of food supplies here."
The man spat to the side. "We don’t care. We’re done with outsiders. Too many leeches coming here, asking for fuel, asking for bikes. We’re not selling anymore. We still have enough food!"
Of course, it was a lie. The man knew that they always needed food supplies. However, he was clearly instructed by Angelo not to accept any trades for the next two weeks.
Kai’s smile didn’t change, but inside, he had already confirmed that man’s location and the fact that there weren’t any other people guarding this entrance...
For a moment, he took a deep breath...
He remembered Angelo’s earlier threats, weeks ago, the man had made it clear that Freedom Shelter was on his list.
Angelo had bikes, fuel, and men who were eyeing their shelter. That alone made him dangerous. If left unchecked, he would eventually strike.
Soon, the rest of the group felt that Kai was about to give his command to attack. Everyone held their weapons tightly...
However, Ralph muttered under his breath, "This doesn’t feel right."
It was as if he had noticed something off.
Still, Kai raised a hand...
"We’re not here to trade. Like I said, we’re scouting. This swamp looks promising for a shelter. Fog for cover, there’s water nearby... it has potential."
The man scoffed. "Potential? You don’t know what you’re talking about. This place isn’t for you."
Kai’s smile thinned.
"Then perhaps you can show us around," Kai said smoothly. "We’re not enemies. Just survivors, like you."
The man hesitated. His rifle lowered further, but his eyes darted toward the mist behind him. "Wait here," he muttered. "I’ll call the others."
Just like that, Kai watched the man disappear into the fog.
He didn’t stop him. In fact, he wanted him to call for backup.
The reason was simple... It was better to fight here, in the open swamp, than to storm a fortified shelter where Angelo’s men would have every advantage.
If they could thin out Haven‐28’s numbers now, the raid would be far easier later.
Kai turned to his companions...
"Stay sharp. They’ll be back, and they’ll bring more. Get ready..."
Claire nodded...
Ralph exhaled slowly. "So we’re baiting them out..."
They already discussed that this could happen, and none of them were surprised.
"Exactly," Kai replied. "I thought it wasn’t possible... Thankfully, we can fight them here, on our terms."

Soon, the strike force moved around, taking positions along the path. Atom stood at the center, like a normal human, because of what he was wearing from head to toe... Atom even had a helmet, so as long as you’re not looking at Atom’s face, you won’t even realize that it was a Sentinel.
Mei crouched low, adjusting her scope. Sera and Althea flanked left and right with their rifles raised.
Alfie, with his Gladiator Talent, was also ready to be in the front lines... He remained silent but ready...
Meanwhile, Noli and the ten workers spread out, forming a defensive line. They looked a little nervous, but the protective gear and rifles gave them confidence.
Furthermore, Kai reminded them of their utilities...
Flashbang grenades, smoke grenades, and a decoy emitter device... He had already handed them to his companions and they should be prepared to use it already.
Still, Kai reminded them again with a low voice...
"Flashbangs first," Kai instructed. "Blind them, disorient them. Smoke for cover. Decoy emitter goes last... make them think we’re more than we are."
Mei smirked. "Classic misdirection."
The group settled into cover, crouching behind reeds and broken logs.
The fog was thick, but it worked both ways.
However, they had thermal detection goggles! This device from the Stealth Gift Pack could give them a clearer view of the situation.
Minutes passed. Then, faint voices echoed through the mist.
"They’re up ahead." The man from before said...
"Leader said no trades. Drive them off."
As they confirmed the presence of the enemies, it didn’t take long before figures emerged... five men at first with their rifles raised within the fog.
More followed, until nearly a dozen stood before Kai’s group.
The tall man from earlier stepped forward, sneering. "You should’ve left. This swamp isn’t yours."
Kai’s smile was cold. "We’re not leaving."
The man raised his rifle. "Then you’ll die here."
Kai’s hand turned upward. "Now!"
Everyone happened so quickly!
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Flashbangs exploded, blinding light tearing through the fog.
The enemy staggered with their rifles dropping as they shielded their eyes.
Then, as if the fog wasn’t enough, smoke grenades hissed!
Thicker clouds started rolling across the swamp. Then, almost at the same time, the decoy emitter was activated, projecting false gunfire and movement deeper into the mist.
Chaos erupted instantly.
Claire fired, her shot precise, dropping one of the blinded men.
Ralph followed, and his rifle was fired as another human survivor fell. Sera and Althea moved in sync, covering the flanks as they also started shooting...
Well, killing humans wasn’t really something they wanted to happen since the enemies were the A.I. Army.
However, since the leader of this shelter threatened to take over their home... Then that was a different conversation.
Mei’s scope flashed as she also began her hunt... one shot, one kill.
The workers fired in bursts...
Even Atom charged ahead! Almost instantly, its mechanical arms smashed aside two enemies who dared to come forward!
The swamp became a battlefield!

sentences.text: Mei, Claire, and the rest of the group couldn’t help but pause after hearing Kai’s words.
His lie was obvious but they didn’t speak...
’Build a shelter, huh...’Claire wryly smiled as she waited for the other side’s response.
Unexpectedly, the man in the fog lowered his rifle slightly, but his suspicion lingered in his stance.
Soon, however, his voice carried frustration more than hostility.
"Tch... another one.
Build a shelter?
Dream on.
You people keep coming here, thinking you can trade or settle.
We told you already!
We’re not accepting trades anymore, and this Mist Mountain is ours!"
Kai tilted his head, as he thought of just going with the flow...
"Wow...
You already claimed this place and you’re not accepting trades?
That’s unusual.
Survivors need supplies.
Fuel, food, weapons... surely you’re still dealing with some fuel?
We have a lot of food supplies here."
The man spat to the side.
"We don’t care.
We’re done with outsiders.
Too many leeches coming here, asking for fuel, asking for bikes.
We’re not selling anymore.
We still have enough food!"
Of course, it was a lie.
The man knew that they always needed food supplies.
However, he was clearly instructed by Angelo not to accept any trades for the next two weeks.
Kai’s smile didn’t change, but inside, he had already confirmed that man’s location and the fact that there weren’t any other people guarding this entrance...

He remembered Angelo’s earlier threats, weeks ago, the man had made it clear that Freedom Shelter was on his list.
Angelo had bikes, fuel, and men who were eyeing their shelter.
That alone made him dangerous.
If left unchecked, he would eventually strike.
Soon, the rest of the group felt that Kai was about to give his command to attack.
Everyone held their weapons tightly...
However, Ralph muttered under his breath, "This doesn’t feel right."
It was as if he had noticed something off.

"We’re not here to trade.
Like I said, we’re scouting.
This swamp looks promising for a shelter.
Fog for cover, there’s water nearby... it has potential."

"Potential?
You don’t know what you’re talking about.
This place isn’t for you."
Kai’s smile thinned.
"Then perhaps you can show us around," Kai said smoothly.
"We’re not enemies.
Just survivors, like you."
The man hesitated.
His rifle lowered further, but his eyes darted toward the mist behind him.

"I’ll call the others."

He didn’t stop him.
In fact, he wanted him to call for backup.
The reason was simple...
It was better to fight here, in the open swamp, than to storm a fortified shelter where Angelo’s men would have every advantage.
If they could thin out Haven‐28’s numbers now, the raid would be far easier later.
Kai turned to his companions...
"Stay sharp.
They’ll be back, and they’ll bring more.
Get ready..."
Claire nodded...
Ralph exhaled slowly.
"So we’re baiting them out..."
They already discussed that this could happen, and none of them were surprised.
"Exactly," Kai replied.
"I thought it wasn’t possible...
Thankfully, we can fight them here, on our terms."

chapters.title: Chapter 217: The Mutants
paragraphs: The group that was meant to send away their visitors was shocked...
Almost in an instant, five people in their group were incapacitated.
"Where are they?! How many?!"
"They’re everywhere!"
The attack happened so swiftly...
Furthermore, the decoy emitter worked perfectly, making them believe Kai’s force was suddenly larger than it was.
Kai advanced through the smoke...
He fired twice, dropping two more. This seemed so easy, but it was all thanks to the flash grenade that they used, disorienting the enemies.
"Push forward! Don’t let them regroup!"
The strike force surged, overwhelming the enemy. In just a few moments, most of Angelo’s men lay dead or incapacitated. The rest stumbled back, retreating into the fog.
Kai raised his hand, signaling a halt.
"Hold. Don’t chase. Let them run."
They had basically announced their presence now... Soon, Angelo’s main forces should come.
"They have a truckload of fuel in their base, it could be very dangerous. I don’t want that damaged. Let’s wait for them here..." Kai said, revealing his true thoughts...
"Ahh... No wonder." Mei gently nodded as she realized that it wasn’t just because their shelter would be hard to siege.
"Now that you said it... You’re right. Let’s just stay here." Claire agreed as she also didn’t want a stray bullet to cause a huge explosion.
No matter how high their level was, an explosion of a fuel truck close to them could still damage their bodies.
Soon, the group regrouped...
The swamp was littered with bodies, but unfortunately, they could not be looted.
"They’ll be back." Ralph muttered as he prepared another flash grenade and smoke grenade, so he could use them swiftly once the enemies got closer.
Kai nodded. "That’s what we want. Angelo will know we’re here now and I hope he sends more..."
Just like that, the strike force tightened its formation. Then, they monitored the fog, ensuring that they wouldn’t get surrounded.
"At this next fight... There’s no need for talking or negotiation... We’ll eliminate them fast." Kai reminded.
The group nodded, as they were all determined to remove these neighboring threats!
As the group waited, Atom stood at the center...
It was the main tank of their squad after all.
The others also found a cover, as they could still die from gunshots...
Minutes passed. Then, faint sounds broke the silence... engines.
Kai nodded as he heard this...
"Motorbikes."
The roar grew louder, echoing through the swamp.
Soon, beams of light were cutting through the fog.
Angelo’s forces weren’t retreating... they were charging forward, and they were coming fast.
The strike force braced. Smoke grenades were readied, and their flashbangs were primed.
Suddenly, the bikes burst through the fog with mud spraying as riders swerved along the narrow path.
Rifles were then fired from the backs of the bikes!
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Bullets started tearing through trees and splintering wood.
The speed and mobility caught Kai’s group off guard.
"Cover!" Kai shouted.
Meanwhile, Atom moved forward, intercepting two bikes with a crushing blow.
Thud! Thud!
The riders flew off, crashing into the mud.
Claire also fired, dropping another rider mid‐turn.
Ralph, who had the Sharpshooter Talent, also started eliminating those he could see from a distance... However, the bikes were fast, and they were unpredictable.
Mei cursed under her breath. "They’re using the swamp and the fog really well..."
Kai’s mind raced. Angelo’s forces were used to this battlefield, and they were striking with mobility, using their bikes to harass and attack from different angles.
Then, the fog shifted... and something else emerged.
Figures stepped out...
They were larger than men, and looking at their silhouettes, they seemed monstrous.
As they charged ahead, they noticed four glowing eyes piercing the mist.
What made them even more shocked were their tails that lashed violently!
Kai froze. "What...?"
Jonathan and Wesley led the charge with their mutated forms...
Perhaps, due to the balance of their bodies, their movements seemed unnatural.
Then, behind them, more mutants appeared... nine others.
Each of them received some sort of mutation from the serum that they had taken...
They were all carrying strange traits like hardened scales, extra eyes, longer tails, more joints, protruding bones, and others...
The strike force was momentarily stunned since they didn’t expect to see monster-like creatures attacking them.
They hadn’t expected any of this.
Mei was the first to react. "Mutants... they have mutants! Careful!"
Jonathan roared with his tail, smashing into a broken tree, splintering it instantly.
Wesley also moved like a predator with his whip‐like tail... His elongated arms reached forward in an attempt to put down Atom but then, he realized that it was a Sentinel!
"Boss! That one in front is a machine! Plasma that thing!"
They do not have unlimited Plasma Charges, so they were only being used against tricky opponents. In normal cases, they just use their bows, guns, and throwing knives.
Soon, Atom was bombarded at all sides.
Meanwhile, the workers panicked at the sight of the monstrous mutants as they started firing wildly.
Bullets struck, but the mutants barely flinched. Their hardened scales deflected shots and those thick muscles absorbed impacts.
Kai frowned. He didn’t expect that Angelo’s threat was far greater than he imagined.
"Flashbangs!" he shouted.
Grenades flew, exploding in bursts of light. The mutants staggered with their four eyes blinking rapidly.
Then, smoke rolled across the swamp, obscuring vision.
"Push!" Kai commanded.
The strike force continued attacking as they fired into the confusion...
Soon, Alfie made his move as his Gladiator Talent displayed its power!
His aura suddenly burst in power.
He charged with a blade in hand and struck the nearest mutant!
Indeed, he clashed with a mutant covered in hardened scales!
His blade smashed into its shoulder, and the scales cracked under his assault.
"Gladiator’s Wrath!" Alfie roared his skill as if it would become even stronger...
Nonetheless, his strikes were so fierce that even the monstrous mutant staggered!
Meanwhile, Jonathan and Wesley were already working together to bring Atom down!

chapters.title: Chapter 218: Troublesome Mutants
paragraphs: Seeing the two Mutants charging ahead, Atom gripped its weapon tightly.
It wasn’t a sharp blade, but a dull, massive sword made of special alloy. The sword was heavy and sturdy, built for smashing rather than slicing.
When Atom swung it, the air itself seemed to tremble.
Wham!
The sword slammed into Jonathan’s tail, knocking the mutant back several steps.
Jonathan roared in anger... His four eyes were already filled with rage. He tried to counter with his claws, but Atom raised the sword again, blocking the strike with sheer force.
Wesley followed suit as he attacked Atom from behind, but Atom seemed to have an eye at the back of its head!
Thud!
Atom just raised a hand to block Wesley’s punch from his eight-fingered hand!
Meanwhile, Sera and Althea moved in. Both of them carried Gene Weapons...
They were low-grade daggers bound to their very souls. However, despite being low-grade, these blades were infused with their energy.
They wouldn’t rust and maintain sharpness no matter how much they use this.
Sera dashed forward with her dagger, slicing across a mutant’s arm.
Ssaaakk~
The blade cut deeper than any normal weapon could, leaving a bloody wound.
The mutant may have a strong pain tolerance, but it still screamed while stumbling back.
Althea followed... She was more confident to move because of the smoke and mist hiding her presence!
Soon, only her dagger could be seen flashing in the smoke. She struck another mutant in the leg, piercing through hardened skin that was almost like scales!
The mutant staggered with its balance broken.
"Keep attacking! Their vitality is crazy high..." Sera shouted as she could tell that the mutants weren’t weakening.
Yes, they were stumbling, getting pushed back, or even getting injured. However, they were also recovering and staying strong!
"Yes... They’re tanks..." Kai muttered as he scanned the battlefield.
Soon, he also called out for his Gene Weapon, the Specter Edge...
It was a spirit‐infused dagger, bound to him alone.
He soon charged at a mutant with protruding bones. With his Specter Step, he swiftly reached the mutant’s side...
"Ha!"
His dagger pierced its chest, as it cut through the leather armor and flesh.
This weapon may be better when used against the A.I. Army because of its special effect, but its sharpness and durability were still great against the mutants...
Just like that, Kai pressed the attack, stabbing again.
The others didn’t slow down as they also followed Kai’s rhythm!
Ralph stayed low with his rifle...
His Sharpshooter Talent allowed him to aim with perfect precision. Even through the fog, his bullets found their marks.
One shot pierced a mutant’s eye. Another dropped a biker mid‐turn...
Meanwhile, Mei vanished into the mist, her Living Camouflage Talent making her invisible.
She reappeared behind a mutant and ambushed him with her rifle!
The enemy fell, before it could turn around and counter...
Then, she disappeared again, blending into the swamp!
Apparently, even if these mutants became physically strong and obtained high vitality, they didn’t have special Gene Skills that could help them maximize their mutations...
Perhaps, if they had enough time to get stronger and obtain proper Gene Skills or even Gene Weapons, they would be terrifying opponents.
However, that wasn’t the case this time.
Soon, even Claire became a problem for them...
She didn’t even have to use her Spirit Possession...
Her passive gene skills already pushed her strength to a mutant level!
Furthermore, she aimed for weak points, cutting tendons, piercing joints. Every move was designed to cripple the enemy.
"I know... I know... I’m doing some unnecessary moves, but that’s because of the fog and the swap, you know!" Claire complained as if she were talking to someone.
However, there was truly no one behind her... Only she could see the one she was talking to.
Suddenly, she felt a strong wave of energy coming to her side.
It was at this time that she realized that Alfie was showing off his Gladiator Talent!
"Gladiator’s Wrath!"
She heard Alfie’s roar as he charged forward...
Then, the battle became bloody really soon as the workers were suddenly overwhelmed by the bikers as they started shooting bows and firing their revolvers.
It seemed that they also regained various resources after the Global Event, allowing them to possess more ammunition for their guns.
Thud! Thud!
"Ohh... Do it, Atom! Destroy them!" Ralph celebrated after seeing Atom swing its dull sword again, smashing Wesley into the mud.
Wesley growled like a beast... Soon, his whip‐like tail lashed out, but Atom blocked with its massive blade.
Kai knew that Atom could win this but he didn’t like how this battle was taking too long.
Without any more hesitation, Kai invoked Specter Step... His body blurring into the smoke. He reappeared behind a mutant and raised his palm...
’Spirit Pulse...’
Energy surged from his palm, blasting the creature back.
Boom!
It crashed into a tree, and splinters started flying everywhere!
The workers then fired their rifles with their bullets tearing through the fog. Some mutants flinched, others shrugged off the shots, but the constant fire kept them distracted.
"Two more..."
Kai’s Keen Sense picked up every movement.
Then, he frowned as he felt some dangerous...
Thankfully, his Bronze Skin was strong enough, and it deflected stray bullets...
Of course, Plasma Shots were still too much for him, but it was fine...
The fight dragged on, but Kai’s strike force didn’t slow down...

Atom swung its dull sword, smashing Wesley into the mud, breaking most of its bones... Jonathan, who seemed to have so many lives, tried to counter, but Kai’s Specter Edge flashed, stabbing deep into his chest.
"It must be the heart, right?" Kai frowned as he really felt impressed with this person’s vitality.
Thankfully, he was right... The mutant roared and made a few steps back before collapsing.
Seeing this, Kai shouted. "Just the riders now! Kill them all!"
Sera and Althea fought bravely with their daggers, but both were injured in the end...
Sera’s arm was slashed, and Althea took a heavy blow to her side.
Furthermore, Ralph fired from cover, but a stray shot grazed his shoulder, leaving him wounded.
The workers, on the other hand, also held their ground, but three of them fell under the bikers’ gunfire...
Nonetheless, just a few minutes after the death of the mutants, Angelo’s forces were also beaten.
"Seriously... Those mutants made this more difficult than I expected." Kai muttered as he looked at the corpses.

However, that wasn’t the case this time.
Soon, even Claire became a problem for them...
She didn’t even have to use her Spirit Possession...
Her passive gene skills already pushed her strength to a mutant level!
Furthermore, she aimed for weak points, cutting tendons, piercing joints.
Every move was designed to cripple the enemy.
"I know...
I know...
I’m doing some unnecessary moves, but that’s because of the fog and the swap, you know!" Claire complained as if she were talking to someone.
However, there was truly no one behind her...
Only she could see the one she was talking to.
Suddenly, she felt a strong wave of energy coming to her side.
It was at this time that she realized that Alfie was showing off his Gladiator Talent!
"Gladiator’s Wrath!"
She heard Alfie’s roar as he charged forward...
Then, the battle became bloody really soon as the workers were suddenly overwhelmed by the bikers as they started shooting bows and firing their revolvers.
It seemed that they also regained various resources after the Global Event, allowing them to possess more ammunition for their guns.
Thud!
Thud!
"Ohh...
Do it, Atom!
Destroy them!" Ralph celebrated after seeing Atom swing its dull sword again, smashing Wesley into the mud.
Wesley growled like a beast...
Soon, his whip‐like tail lashed out, but Atom blocked with its massive blade.
Kai knew that Atom could win this but he didn’t like how this battle was taking too long.
Without any more hesitation, Kai invoked Specter Step...
His body blurring into the smoke.
He reappeared behind a mutant and raised his palm...
’Spirit Pulse...’
Energy surged from his palm, blasting the creature back.
Boom!
It crashed into a tree, and splinters started flying everywhere!
The workers then fired their rifles with their bullets tearing through the fog.
Some mutants flinched, others shrugged off the shots, but the constant fire kept them distracted.
"Two more..."
Kai’s Keen Sense picked up every movement.
Then, he frowned as he felt some dangerous...
Thankfully, his Bronze Skin was strong enough, and it deflected stray bullets...
Of course, Plasma Shots were still too much for him, but it was fine...
The fight dragged on, but Kai’s strike force didn’t slow down...
Atom swung its dull sword, smashing Wesley into the mud, breaking most of its bones...
Jonathan, who seemed to have so many lives, tried to counter, but Kai’s Specter Edge flashed, stabbing deep into his chest.
"It must be the heart, right?" Kai frowned as he really felt impressed with this person’s vitality.
Thankfully, he was right...
The mutant roared and made a few steps back before collapsing.
Seeing this, Kai shouted.
"Just the riders now!
Kill them all!"
Sera and Althea fought bravely with their daggers, but both were injured in the end...
Sera’s arm was slashed, and Althea took a heavy blow to her side.
Furthermore, Ralph fired from cover, but a stray shot grazed his shoulder, leaving him wounded.
The workers, on the other hand, also held their ground, but three of them fell under the bikers’ gunfire...
Nonetheless, just a few minutes after the death of the mutants, Angelo’s forces were also beaten.
"Seriously...
Those mutants made this more difficult than I expected." Kai muttered as he looked at the corpses.

chapters.title: Chapter 219: The Interesting Stat
paragraphs: As the battle ended, everyone started resting for a bit as they felt exhausted after the adrenaline rush was gone.
Furthermore, the Foreign Survivor’s Spirit Points were at their lowest as well.
However, it didn’t take long before everyone started working together to clear up the battlefield.
Soon, Kai found a familiar figure...
It was Angelo himself!
The man was bloodied, his body pinned under his own motorbike. He tried to move, but the weight crushed him down. His breath was already shallow, and his eyes were filled with fear.
Just like that, the man who had once threatened Freedom Shelter was about to die. There was no big or special fight against him or any dramatic ending.
It was a useless death.
Kai didn’t feel much. Even if Angelo was a fellow human, in this world, it didn’t matter. The apocalypse had changed everything.
The A.I. Rebellion had filled the land with mechanical soldiers, and survivors had turned against each other. Resources, jealousy, and greed made enemies out of people who should have been allies.
Angelo had chosen that path, and now he was gone.
"Loot them before the fire spreads," Kai ordered after seeing some small fires starting to spread.
Just like that, the group moved quickly. They stripped weapons, ammo, and supplies from the fallen.
Anything left behind would be burned or lost.
Those uninjured worked swiftly with steady hands, knowing how important it was to obtain these items. After all, they knew that Kai wouldn’t be with them at all times.
When the looting was done, Kai led them toward the shelter.
The fog grew thinner, and soon the buildings of Haven‐28 came into view.
Although there was a fence, it was not enough to block their path...
They easily entered the place as Atom opened the metal gate...
Inside, they found the survivors.

Twelve people in total, who were men and women. They weren’t fighters, and even without asking, Kai could tell from their calloused hands that they were workers. They were definitely assigned to farming, sewing, cooking, and cleaning.
"They were laborers, not warriors."
Kai studied them silently. These people weren’t a threat.
They were weak, tired, and scared. They had no weapons or any talents useful for battle.
They were simply trying to live.
"They’re locals," Mei whispered. "Not from Earth."
Kai nodded. That explained their simple lives.
They hadn’t been transported like him and the others...
They had always been here, surviving in their own way.
The twelve looked at Kai’s strike force with wide eyes. They didn’t resist. They knew the fighters were gone, and only workers remained.
Kai lowered his weapon.
"The battle is over," he said quietly. "This Haven‐28 has fallen..."
The group stood in silence.
What else could they do?
They could only submit to their new leaders. Well, they weren’t fighters, and they knew their worth.
By now, they knew that the Foreign Survivors were here to fight back against the A.I. Rebel, Aria. Their enemies weren’t really fellow humans unless they were threatened.
Because of that, they knew that they just had to be obedient and become useful.
Soon, the twelve looked at each other and made a decision to bow to their new leader.
Kai didn’t make it difficult for these civilians...
He calmly looked at the twelve who bowed their heads.
He lowered his weapon and asked calmly, "What’s the situation here? Tell me everything."
One of the men stepped forward.
He was thin, with tired eyes, but his voice was firm. "My name is Rolly," he said. "I’ll explain."

Rolly pointed toward the misty swamp around them. "This place wasn’t always like this. Before, it was just a foggy town. But one of the Foreign Survivors under Angelo blocked the river in the north. That’s how the swamp was made. It was for protection. Whenever the swamp dried up, they blocked the river again and let the water flow back here."
Kai and the others exchanged surprised looks. They hadn’t expected the swamp to be man‐made.
Rolly continued, "There’s also a truck filled with fuel inside. Angelo kept it hidden. And there are extra motorbikes too, taken from a dealership nearby. That’s how his men moved so fast."
Kai nodded slowly. "What about food?"

Rolly sighed. "I’m a baker. We still have flour, and I’ve been cultivating wild yeast so we can make bread. But the wheat is running out. Soon, we won’t be able to bake anymore. We’ll have to rely on mushrooms and whatever else the forest can give us."

Kai understood their situation. These people weren’t loyal to Angelo... they were just surviving. He thought about bringing them back to Freedom Shelter. But first, he wanted to know their true strength.
He pulled out his Status Crystals.
The glowing shards lit up in his hand. He placed one before Rolly...
"Touch it..."
Rolly wasn’t sure what it was, but he followed him nonetheless. He didn’t feel any hostility from Kai anyway...
Soon, he was shocked by his own status...
[ Name: Rolly ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 4 ]
[ Spirit: 20 / 20 ]
[ Physique Rating: E- ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: None ]
"Is this my status? I heard Angelo and others talking about this." He muttered.
Kai just nodded at him and asked for the next person to be checked. After all, if someone was quite special with an interesting skill or stat, then he wouldn’t mind nurturing them.
However, after checking five more people, he didn’t find anyone with decent stat...
As he was thinking that no one here would give him a surprise, the sixth person, who was supposed to be the shelter’s seamstress, showed him an interesting stat!
[ Name: Galatea ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 5 ]
[ Spirit: 45 / 65 ]
[ Physique Rating: E ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Needlecraft Lv0, Meridian Touch Lv0 ]
[ Needlecraft (Level 0): Improves sewing and repairing ability. Allows faster crafting of cloth armor and minor reinforcement of fabric. Slightly increases the durability of stitched items. ]
[ Meridian Touch (Level 0): Uses basic acupuncture techniques. Can ease pain, reduce fatigue, and slightly boost recovery when applied to allies. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 220: Skilled Workers and the Side Project
paragraphs: Kai’s eyes lit up when he saw Galatea’s result.
Two passive skills... one for sewing and one for acupuncture. That was rare.
He smiled faintly, but he didn’t stop there. He wanted to see if there were more surprises.
Just like that, he continued checking the rest of the survivors.
Most of them were ordinary, with no special talents. Farmers, cleaners, cooks. Useful, but not remarkable. Then, one more caught his attention.
His name was Silas.
[ Name: Silas ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 7 ]
[ Spirit: 50 / 50 ]
[ Physique Rating: E ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Gearhand Lv1, Engine Sense Lv0, Salvager’s Instinct Lv0 ]
[ Gearhand (Level 1): Improves efficiency in repairing and maintaining machines. Reduces time needed to fix mechanical tools and vehicles. ]
[ Engine Sense (Level 0): Grants basic intuition for diagnosing problems in engines and generators. Slightly increases success rate when restoring damaged machinery. ]
[ Salvager’s Instinct (Level 0): Enhances ability to dismantle mechanical items and reuse parts. Slightly improves yield when salvaging A.I. soldier components. ]
Kai couldn’t help but feel impressed with this person.
"Three passive skills... all related to mechanics. You’re amazing..."

Silas scratched the back of his neck, looking a little embarrassed. "I got lucky and had a few sips of a gene enhancement liquid... Anyway, I was always been the one taking care of the generator here. The motorbikes too. And when we fought the A.I. soldiers, I dismantled them. Their parts were useful for blades, tools, and other things. Of course, I had help from some of Angelo’s Foreign Survivors. They had skills too, so together we managed to make weapons."
Kai nodded, impressed. "That’s valuable. Mechanics are rare. You’ve been keeping this place alive."
Silas gave a small smile. "I did what I could. But... there’s something else."
Kai tilted his head. "Go on."
Silas hesitated, then spoke.

"In my free time, I’ve been working on a side project. I wanted to gain control of the Sentinels. I tried hacking them. If I could turn them against the A.I. Rebel, we’d have powerful allies. But... my knowledge isn’t enough. I don’t have the right tools, and I don’t know enough programming. Whenever I activate one, it still obeys the A.I. Rebel. I’m stuck. Angelo had given up on this side project, but I think that we just need the right person to head this project."
Kai’s lips curved into a smile. "That’s ambitious. And maybe possible."
He glanced at Mei, who was listening quietly.

"We’re both programmers. With your mechanical skills and our coding, we might be able to make progress. Not now, but later. For now, just keep your notes and your parts safe. We’ll do something about it."
Silas’s eyes widened. "You mean... you’ll help?"
Kai nodded firmly. "Yes. If we work together, we might succeed."

Indeed, Kai already had a few items he needed to complete this project. He wasn’t sure how far Silas had gone with this, but with his technical skills and the circuit boards in his possession, it might be possible.
Silas looked relieved. It seemed that his dream wasn’t impossible.
Kai then turned his attention back to Galatea, the seamstress.
She was standing quietly with her hands folded in front of her.
She looked nervous...
"Galatea," Kai said gently. "Tell me more about your acupuncture techniques."
She blinked, surprised that he was interested.

"It’s simple, really. I learned it from my grandmother. She taught me how to use special needles to ease pain. Well, they’re different from the ones in my work... But I can press certain points to reduce fatigue, help someone sleep, or calm their breathing. It’s not strong healing, but it helps."
Kai nodded. "That’s useful..."
Galatea continued as she realized that Kai was genuinely interested about her skills.
She wasn’t really talking about this with other people, so talking to someone with the same interest made her a little happy...

"I’ve used it on the workers here. When they were too tired from farming, I eased their muscles. When someone had headaches, I pressed the points to relieve them. It doesn’t cure wounds, but it helps the body recover faster."
Kai leaned closer...
"Can you show me?"
As he said this, Claire and everyone else who were looking around also got curious. None of them had ever seen these ancient techniques after all.
They might have heard of it or seen it in the movies, but never in real life.
It was the same for Kai. According to what he heard, it shouldn’t be a painful experience. And since Galatea had the Gene Skill to back it up, he felt a bit more at ease to get tested...
After seeing so many people looking at them, Galatea felt a little nervous and hesitated... But then, she pulled out a small pouch.
Inside were thin needles, carefully wrapped.
"Uhm... I’m not sure if I should try it on you." Galatea said after seeing Kai removing his cloak.
Kai paused, but before he could insist, Galatea stepped toward one of the injured workers who had a strained shoulder.
She spoke gently while gesturing at the man, "Please, let me treat him instead."
Kai nodded, putting his cloak back on. "Alright..."
Just like that, Galatea instructed the man.
"Please, sit down. Relax your shoulders."
The man obeyed, lowering himself onto a wooden stool nearby.
Galatea placed a hand on his arm to steady him.
"Lean forward a little," she said, making sure he was comfortable.
Only then did she prepare the needle. With gentle hands, she pressed it into a point near the man’s neck.
The worker winced at first, then sighed in relief. His shoulders loosened, and his breathing grew calmer.
"It feels... lighter," he whispered.
Kai watched closely. "So it works."
Galatea nodded. "It’s not magic. It’s just technique. But combined with rest and food, it helps people recover faster."
Kai nodded as he felt satisfied with this performance.
"Galatea," Kai said firmly, "your skill is important. You’ll be helping us from now on... No, all of you will be part of my Clan to some degree. To celebrate that, we’ll have a feast tonight!"
Just like that, while Victor and the others were busy trying to build the Barrier Generator, Kai and the others were here celebrating...

chapters.title: Chapter 221: The Special Item
paragraphs: A few hours earlier, before Kai and his team arrived at the Haven-28 shelter, Victor had been busy with his own task.
Apparently, after the Surveillance Sweep Event, it had been decided that he would be the one to learn the blueprint once it was completed.
Because of that, everyone handed over their fragments. Ten pieces were required, but they had managed to gather more than that...
Still, with the ten complete fragments, they were able to obtain a complete blueprint...
Since Victor had mechanical talent, it was decided that he would be the one to learn this precious device blueprint. He had the hands and the mind for it anyway...
Victor held the fragments tightly. The system prompt appeared before him...
[ Do you want to learn the Blueprint? ]
[ Warning: Learning this Blueprint will consume the item. Once learned, you will permanently gain the ability to build the Advanced Barrier System Generator, even without prior forging knowledge. ]
[ Note: Items built directly by you will retain system effects. Copies made by ordinary craftsmen will not inherit the additional system effects. ]
Victor didn’t hesitate. "Yes," he said firmly.

The fragments dissolved into light, merging into his mind. Knowledge flooded him instantly. He now understood the design, the structure, and the materials needed. It was as if he had studied the blueprint for years.
He exhaled slowly. "I know how to build it."
The Guild gathered around him, curious. Victor opened the system window again, listing the required materials. His eyes scanned the list carefully.
First was the Barrier Core Stabilizer, a vital piece that would keep the generator’s energy flow steady. Without it, the barrier would collapse under its own power.

Next were the Core Parts, intricate mechanical components that would form the skeleton of the generator. These were rare and difficult to craft, but they had already salvaged some from fallen machines.

Then came the energy requirements: 50 C‐Grade Cores and 5 B‐Grade Cores. Victor frowned slightly. "That’s a lot of cores," he muttered. "But it makes sense. The barrier will need immense power to function."
Finally, the most important piece... the Tyrant Furnace. This was the heart of the generator, the device that would refine and channel the cores into usable energy.
Without it, the generator couldn’t even start.
"Thankfully, we already have the furnace. We recycled it after defeating several Tyrant Units before... That battle wasn’t for nothing."
The Guild members nodded.
They remembered the fight well, the towering Field Tyrant, with their heavy armor, and the chaos they had caused.
Defeating them hadn’t been that easy, but now, their remains were proving useful.

Victor continued to study the blueprint. "We’ll need to assemble the stabilizer, attach the core parts, and feed the furnace with the cores. Once it’s complete, the generator will activate and create a barrier strong enough to withstand waves of mechanical soldiers."
"How long will it take?" Wallace asked.
Victor thought for a moment. "If we have all the materials ready, in a few days. But gathering the cores will be the hardest part. Fifty C‐Grade and five B‐Grade... That’s no small task."
Wallace grinned. "Then we’ll just have to hunt more machines."
Victor smiled faintly...
With the Advanced Barrier System Generator, Haven-45, and the Freedom Shelter could become nearly untouchable.
Victor clenched his fists. "We’ll build it. No matter what."
The others nodded in agreement. The path ahead was dangerous, but now they had a clear goal...
Thanks to that, Victor began working on the smaller parts of the machine, and he had been very busy ever since.

In fact, during the Global Event, their artillery had been damaged and was in need of repairs. However, because his priority was fully focused on the Barrier Generator, the artillery was left unattended for the time being.
Another week quickly passed.
During this time, Haven‐28 had stabilized as Kai and Mei stayed behind to ensure its safety.
Claire and the others had already returned to Freedom Shelter and Haven‐45 Shelter, keeping the network of survivors strong.
The week wasn’t without danger.
Sentinels, Swarmers, and other mechanical threats attacked from time to time, but they always came in small numbers. Each raid was quickly dealt with, leaving no serious damage.
Meanwhile, the survivors reinforced their base.
Under Aurora’s careful guidance, the crop fields had improved greatly. The soil was healthier, the plants were stronger, and the yield was already showing signs of growth.
Food security was slowly becoming less of a worry.
Still, one Guild Mission remained incomplete.
They were tasked with recruiting a total of fifteen members, but the foreign survivors here numbered only twelve. It was not enough to finish the mission...
Yet, during this week, something remarkable happened.
"I did it!"
Elena, the nurse from Earth who had awakened a Master‐Grade Artisan Talent after entering this apocalypse, finally completed her work on the golden bull’s horn.
This bull had previously caused some trouble for them and later became food for everyone, which gave a huge boost in Spirit Recovery and others.
Elena could still remember how the other bulls may have been corrupted at that time, but this golden bull was different...
In any case, she had spent days studying the golden bull’s horn, testing its durability, and shaping it precisely how he wanted.
The golden horn was unlike anything she had ever handled before. It glowed faintly, carrying traces of spiritual energy.
With her Artisan Talent guiding her hands, Elena had carved, polished, and reforged it into something extraordinary.
Of course, she only used a small part of it as she felt that many Survivors must benefit from this horn. Furthermore, she was also afraid of making mistakes.
At last, the system window appeared before her eyes...
[ Crafting Complete! ]
[ +50 Experience Points ]
The fifty experience points were a great bonus reward, so Elena felt better. Of course, she was also expecting to craft something nice with such a reward.
Thankfully, she wasn’t wrong.
[ Item Created: Golden Horn Pendant ]
[ Grade: B ]
[ Effect: Increases wearer’s Spirit recovery speed by 15%. Slightly enhances resistance against mental fatigue. ]
[ Additional Effect: Emits a faint aura that calms nearby allies, reducing stress and fear during battle. ]
Elena gasped, her hands trembling as she held the pendant.
"I... I made something so amazing..." she whispered, her voice filled with joy.
Furthermore, with the size of her pendant, she believed that she could create 30 more of these with the golden horns left!

chapters.title: Chapter 223: The X-01 and the Gene Trader
paragraphs: Wallace froze as he also noticed some dark figures getting closer...
As soon as he adjusted his vision, he immediately realized what he was seeing...
When the two figures stepped into view, he also felt a little nervous like Farrah.

At first glance, they looked like Sentinels, the humanoid robots controlled by the A.I. Civilization. Normally, these machines carried standard weapons like rifles or swords. Against such enemies, Farrah would not have hesitated.
She had faced dozens before, cutting them down with her sword skills as a Spirit Knight.
But this time, her grip on the sword tightened, and her expression grew tense.
The Sentinel in front was different. It was actually wearing a Survivor Gear Set!
Furthermore, strapped to its back was a familiar Emergency Thruster Pack, something that they had obtained from Kai!

Across its chest hung a tactical vest, loaded with ammunition magazines. A carbine rifle rested against its shoulder, and an axe was clipped to its side. The vest itself seemed heavy, hinting at more weapons hidden within.
Wallace frowned... "That’s... not normal."
Farrah nodded.
Just like Wallace, she had seen other Sentinels with various equipment, but this one was different. It wasn’t just armed... it was outfitted like a survivor. That was what unsettled her.
She shifted her stance, preparing to unleash her skill.
The glow of Spirit Energy began to gather around her blade. But before she could strike, the Sentinel did something unexpected.
It didn’t raise its rifle. It didn’t aim its axe. Instead, it reached into its vest and pulled out... a folded piece of paper.
"What?" Wallace muttered, stunned.

The Sentinel extended the paper toward them. Farrah hesitated, then lowered her blade slightly. Wallace realized that this Sentinel wasn’t trying to harm them and stepped closer, before he carefully unfolded the sheet.
The message was written in Kai’s handwriting.
[ This is Sentinel X‐01. It will protect the cave entrance, ensuring the safety of the Gene Trader -if there is one inside. - KAI ]
Wallace blinked. "Kai... sent this?"
Kai didn’t even mention anything like this in the Guild Chat!
Farrah exhaled slowly, her tension easing.
The Sentinel stood silently and waited for them to clear the way...
It wasn’t hostile. It was guarding...
They were sure about the exact instructions given to this Sentinel, but soon they cleared a path.
Then, the machine moved to the cave entrance just outside the Alarm System device and positioned itself like a sentry, unmoving, while its glowing optics were scanning the area.
Wallace scratched his head. "Ha... what if there’s no Gene Trader inside?"
Farrah sheathed her sword, her expression was thoughtful.
"Then we report back to Kai through Guild Chat. He must have some way to control it remotely. But still..." She glanced at the Sentinel...
"I didn’t know they could already make Sentinels break free from the A.I. rebel’s control."
Wallace nodded, still staring at the machine. "It’s... impressive. Almost unsettling."
Farrah’s lips curved into a faint smile. "Yes... If Kai and the Guild can truly reprogram Sentinels, then this changes everything. Imagine turning the enemy’s weapons into our guardians."
The thought lingered between them as the cave loomed darker ahead.
Still, the two of them finally realized that their fight against the A.I. rebels might not just be about survival. It might be about control... about who could command the machines.
And Kai had just proven that the Guild was one step closer to that power.
"Let’s investigate," Wallace said, recalling their mission.
"Alright..."
Together, they stepped closer to the cave.
Wallace and Farrah didn’t venture too far into the cave before their eyes adjusted to the dim light. Soon, they spotted a lone figure seated near the wall, cloaked in dark fabric.
Around him were bags, crates, and containers stacked neatly, each one marked with strange symbols.
Without a doubt, this was a Gene Trader.
"Whoa... Amazing..." Wallace muttered.
"Huh? They all looked the same to me." Farrah commented.
Wallace could only helplessly smile as they approached the figure with caution.
"Gene Trader?" Wallace called out. "We want to trade."
Soon, the figure raised his hands slowly, revealing a crystal...
As soon as it appeared, both Wallace and Farrah received a system prompt:
[ Gene Trader’s Store ]
[ Survivor Medal Items ] [ Energy Core Items ]
Their eyes widened, and a rush of relief filled them. They celebrated quietly, exchanging a glance that confirmed their excitement. This was no illusion... they were truly dealing with a Gene Trader.
They had brought Survivor Medals and Energy Cores specifically for this purpose, and now their preparation was paying off.
Wallace selected the Survivor Medal Items and soon, the store window expanded, listing familiar items...
[ Super Gene Enhancement Serum ]
[ Description: A basic serum that slightly improves genetic compatibility, granting small boosts to overall stats and a high chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum ]
[ Description: A rare genetic resource that grants balanced boosts to overall stats and provides a small chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Prime Gene Enhancement Serum ]
[ Description: A rare serum that focuses on greatly improving Physique and provides a small chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Mutagenic Gene Enhancement Serum ]
[ Description: An unstable serum that grants massive boosts to overall stats but carries a high chance of mutation. Mutations may result in unpredictable abilities or severe drawbacks.
Cost: 1 Survivor Medal ]
The price of the four Gene Enhancement Serums was still the same...
Soon, Wallace checked the pills...
[ Gene Stabilization Pill ]
[ Rapid Recovery Pill ]
[ Neural Expansion Pill ]
Seeing that they were all the same and similar prices, Wallace finally felt satisfied...
However, as they scrolled further, they noticed something unusual... something no other Gene Trader had offered before.
[ Gene Weapon (Low‐Grade) ]
[ Description: A weapon forged with genetic resonance. Even at low grade, it synchronizes with the wielder’s Talent, amplifying combat efficiency.
Cost: 10 Survivor Medals ]
[ Gene Weapon (Mid‐Grade) ]
[ Description: A weapon forged with genetic resonance. It greatly synchronizes with the wielder’s Talent, amplifying combat efficiency.
Cost: 30 Survivor Medals ]
"Gene Weapons...?"
Wallace and Farrah couldn’t help but feel impressed.
Of course, the two of them already had low-grade Gene Weapons after receiving the reward from the Surveillance Sweep Event...
However, obtaining more was never a bad thing!

chapters.title: Chapter 224: Haven-28’s Workshop
paragraphs: Farrah’s lips parted slightly... She was amazed by this new set of items being sold by the Gene Trader.
"This is new. I’ve never seen a Gene Trader offer Gene Weapons before."
Wallace nodded since they had seen a couple of Gene Traders by now and none of them were selling dormant Gene Weapons.
Of course, there were other items being sold...
[ Bloodbound Bracelet: A crimson band that absorbs the wearer’s blood and solidifies it into a blade. The weapon’s strength depends on the user’s vitality.
Cost: 5 Survivor Medals ]
[ Phantom Mask: A dark mask that alters facial features and disguises the wearer’s identity. It also dampens breathing sounds, making stealth easier.
Cost: 6 Survivor Medals ]
[ Dire Claw Gauntlet: Crafted from pale skeletal material that reshapes to fit the user’s hand, giving it a rigid, claw-like form.
Cost: 5 Survivor Medals ]
[ Chameleon Cloak: A cloak made of adaptive fibers that blend with the environment, reducing visibility.
Cost: 5 Survivor Medals ]
[ Venomfang Dagger: A curved blade that infuses the user’s blood into its edge, producing a toxic effect. The poison weakens enemies over time.
Cost: 6 Survivor Medals ]
These items seemed to have extraordinary abilities, but they weren’t exactly Gene Weapons. Instead, they were considered Special Weapons.
Because of that, anyone could obtain them, and they could also be stolen...
"Are you going to buy something?" Farrah asked.
"Yes... I have enough for a Serum." Wallace replied as he looked at the cloaked figure who seemed to be waiting for their decision.
Meanwhile, just a couple of days ago, the workshop inside the Haven-28 Shelter remained bright even during the night...
There was a generator in this shelter, giving a steady supply of electricity to run the whole place...
At this time, Silas had cleared a space in his workshop since his side project had to be expanded soon, according to Kai.
He had set up more tables covered with dismantled Sentinel parts... torsos, arms, heads, and circuit boards stacked neatly in rows.
Kai and Mei entered, each carrying their laptops they had obtained from Gene Traders before.
They already had various parts they needed, including the Nano Circuit Boards. They were compact, wafer‐thin replacements designed for regaining control over the Sentinels.
Indeed, unlike the original boards, these were designed to sever the Sentinels’ connection to the A.I. Rebel, Aria.
Silas greeted them with a tired smile.
"You came. Good. I’ve prepared a batch of Sentinels for testing. Ten units, stripped down and waiting."
Kai nodded, his eyes scanning the parts.
"Perfect. Tonight, we’ll see if we can finally break them free."
Mei set her laptop on the table, booting up the interface.
The two of them had already conducted their own studies over the Sentinel’s program, so they were already aware of what they would expect...
"C-Grade Sentinels are impossible... But E-Grade and D-Grade ones weren’t as terrifying as I thought..." Mei muttered while looking at lines of code that scrolled across her screen.
It was the beginnings of a custom program she had been writing for days.
"Yes... We just need to overwrite their firmware completely. The Nano Circuit Boards will handle the hardware side, but the software must be rewritten to block any external signals."

Silas leaned over one of the dismantled heads, pointing at the socket where the old circuit board had been removed. "I’ve already disconnected the uplink modules. Once we slot in the Nano Board, they’ll lose their tether to Aria’s network. But without your program, they’ll just be empty shells."
Kai opened his laptop, syncing with Mei’s. "Then let’s start. I’ll handle the encryption layer. Mei, you focus on the behavioral routines."
Together, they began typing furiously.
It was like back on Earth when they were still working as Systems Engineers.
Just like that, the room echoed with the clatter of keys and the faint hum of cooling fans...
Well, those laptops were working overtime...
Silas watched, fascinated by what they were doing...

He wasn’t a programmer, but he understood machines. He busied himself with the physical work like, removing old boards, cleaning sockets, and preparing the Sentinels for installation. His Gearhand skill made his movements precise, while Salvager’s Instinct ensured he recovered every usable part.
"Mhmm... This isn’t that complicated but... it takes time." Kai muttered.
Well, his program focused on severing connections. He wrote lines of code that blocked wireless signals, disabled uplink ports, and rerouted command pathways to local control only.
"We can’t risk even a single packet reaching Aria," he muttered. "If she senses these units, she’ll override them instantly."
Mei nodded... She knew that a single mistake could let Aria control the Sentinels back...
Nonetheless, she remained confident as she adjusted the behavioral subroutines.
"As for the recognition protocols... Mhmm..."
Mei paused, her fingers hovering over the keyboard.

"You know... the Sentinels already have recognition protocols. They can distinguish humans from machines. That part is built into their sensors... thermal imaging, gait analysis, facial structure. We don’t need to rewrite that."
Silas looked up from the torso he was working on. "So we just use what’s already there?"

Kai nodded. "Exactly. The problem isn’t detection... it’s classification. Aria’s code tells them to treat all humans as targets unless flagged otherwise. We’ll flip that logic. Humans will be neutral by default."

Mei frowned thoughtfully. "I considered building a biometric database for Guild members, but if Aria ever breached the system, she could steal it. That would put everyone at risk. We can’t afford that."
Kai nodded. "No databases. No personal identifiers. We’ll keep it simple. All humans are neutral. The Sentinels won’t attack unless they receive a direct command from us."
Silas scratched his chin. "So they’ll just stand there if someone walks past? Even locals?"

"Yes," Kai said firmly. "That way, there’s no chance of them mistaking civilians for enemies. The only exception will be Aria’s machines. Their signals and hardware profiles are distinct. We’ll hard‐code those as hostile."
Mei typed quickly, adjusting the subroutines. "Alright. Default behavior... Humans are neutral... Aria’s machines are hostile, and commands are only accepted from whitelisted devices."
Just like that, the three worked together all day until the first Sentinel under their care was born...
"Let’s call it Sentinel... Codename: X-01."
