Kai and Mei entered, each carrying their laptops they had obtained from Gene Traders before.
They already had various parts they needed, including the Nano Circuit Boards.
They were compact, wafer‐thin replacements designed for regaining control over the Sentinels.
Indeed, unlike the original boards, these were designed to sever the Sentinels’ connection to the A.I.
Rebel, Aria.
Silas greeted them with a tired smile.
"You came.
Good.
I’ve prepared a batch of Sentinels for testing.
Ten units, stripped down and waiting."
Kai nodded, his eyes scanning the parts.
"Perfect.
Tonight, we’ll see if we can finally break them free."
Mei set her laptop on the table, booting up the interface.
The two of them had already conducted their own studies over the Sentinel’s program, so they were already aware of what they would expect...
"C-Grade Sentinels are impossible...
But E-Grade and D-Grade ones weren’t as terrifying as I thought..." Mei muttered while looking at lines of code that scrolled across her screen.
It was the beginnings of a custom program she had been writing for days.
"Yes...
We just need to overwrite their firmware completely.
The Nano Circuit Boards will handle the hardware side, but the software must be rewritten to block any external signals."
Silas leaned over one of the dismantled heads, pointing at the socket where the old circuit board had been removed.
"I’ve already disconnected the uplink modules.
Once we slot in the Nano Board, they’ll lose their tether to Aria’s network.
But without your program, they’ll just be empty shells."
Kai opened his laptop, syncing with Mei’s.
"Then let’s start.
I’ll handle the encryption layer.
Mei, you focus on the behavioral routines."
Together, they began typing furiously.
It was like back on Earth when they were still working as Systems Engineers.
Just like that, the room echoed with the clatter of keys and the faint hum of cooling fans...
Well, those laptops were working overtime...
Silas watched, fascinated by what they were doing...
He wasn’t a programmer, but he understood machines.
He busied himself with the physical work like, removing old boards, cleaning sockets, and preparing the Sentinels for installation.
His Gearhand skill made his movements precise, while Salvager’s Instinct ensured he recovered every usable part.
"Mhmm...
This isn’t that complicated but... it takes time." Kai muttered.
Well, his program focused on severing connections.
He wrote lines of code that blocked wireless signals, disabled uplink ports, and rerouted command pathways to local control only.
"We can’t risk even a single packet reaching Aria," he muttered.
"If she senses these units, she’ll override them instantly."
Mei nodded...
She knew that a single mistake could let Aria control the Sentinels back...
Nonetheless, she remained confident as she adjusted the behavioral subroutines.
"As for the recognition protocols...
Mhmm..."
Mei paused, her fingers hovering over the keyboard.
"You know... the Sentinels already have recognition protocols.
They can distinguish humans from machines.
That part is built into their sensors... thermal imaging, gait analysis, facial structure.
We don’t need to rewrite that."
Silas looked up from the torso he was working on.
"So we just use what’s already there?"
Kai nodded.
"Exactly.
The problem isn’t detection... it’s classification.
Aria’s code tells them to treat all humans as targets unless flagged otherwise.
We’ll flip that logic.
Humans will be neutral by default."
Mei frowned thoughtfully.
"I considered building a biometric database for Guild members, but if Aria ever breached the system, she could steal it.
That would put everyone at risk.
We can’t afford that."
Kai nodded.
"No databases.
No personal identifiers.
We’ll keep it simple.
All humans are neutral.
The Sentinels won’t attack unless they receive a direct command from us."
Silas scratched his chin.
"So they’ll just stand there if someone walks past?
Even locals?"
"Yes," Kai said firmly.
"That way, there’s no chance of them mistaking civilians for enemies.
The only exception will be Aria’s machines.
Their signals and hardware profiles are distinct.
We’ll hard‐code those as hostile."
Mei typed quickly, adjusting the subroutines.
"Alright.
Default behavior...
Humans are neutral...
Aria’s machines are hostile, and commands are only accepted from whitelisted devices."
Just like that, the three worked together all day until the first Sentinel under their care was born...
"Let’s call it Sentinel...
Codename: X-01."

chapters.title: Chapter 225: Level Cap
paragraphs: Silas installed the first Nano Circuit Board into a Sentinel’s chest cavity. The board clicked into place, and soon, its faint glow started spreading across the machine’s frame.
"Board installed," Silas reported. "Ready for activation."
Kai and Mei exchanged a glance. Kai pressed a key, sending the new program into the Sentinel’s core. The machine’s optics blinked, then glowed a steady blue.
[ Sentinel Unit Reprogrammed ]
[ Status: Independent Control Established ]
"Let’s call it Sentinel... Codename: X-01." Kai muttered as he programmed its new codename.
[ Designation: Sentinel X‐01 ]
Soon, Silas gasped... "It worked...!"
After all, whenever he activated a Sentinel before, they would immediately try to kill him. This time, however, it didn’t attack!
"Stand up..." Kai muttered.
The Sentinel heard the instruction and straightened itself as its gears started smoothly.
It didn’t move aggressively and listened to instructions really well... Then, it stood silently awaiting orders...
Kai smiled faintly. "X‐01. Our first success."
Mei leaned on her chair as she felt suddenly exhausted. She was proud of her work but she had no time to enjoy it yet.
"We’ll need to test its behavior in the field. But for now, it’s stable. We should rest for a bit..."
Silas’s hands trembled as he touched the machine’s armored plating. "I’ve dreamed of this for months... and now it’s real."

Kai placed a hand on his shoulder. "This is just the beginning. With your mechanical skills and our programming, we can reprogram entire batches. Imagine dozens of Sentinels guarding the Shelter, patrolling the perimeter, fighting alongside us..."
Silas nodded vigorously. "I’ll prepare the rest. Ten units tonight, more tomorrow."
He actually had it rough... After all, he had to assemble these Sentinels.
Apparently, the Sentinels in the warehouse were all defeated by Angelo and his team... while some of them were just looted from the junkyard.
It means they all had damaged parts because of the battle they had gone through.
It was unlike the New Haven-45 with so many of these Sentinels that had zero damage. They just needed some battery charge or replacements.
"Don’t worry, Silas... In a few days, we will have intact Sentinels. You won’t have to assemble them."
For now, however, they moved quickly as they planned to make as many X versions of Sentinels as they could.
Silas installed boards, Kai encrypted pathways, Mei rewrote routines. One by one, the Sentinels came online...
[ Sentinel Unit Reprogrammed ]
[ Status: Independent Control Established ]
[ Designation: Sentinel X‐02 ]
[ Sentinel Unit Reprogrammed ]
[ Status: Independent Control Established ]
[ Designation: Sentinel X‐03 ]
By dawn, six units stood silently in the workshop, awaiting orders.
The three of them stood together, staring at the reprogrammed Sentinels. They still couldn’t believe it... they had done something so incredible.
Over the next few days, the workshop never truly fell silent.
The clatter of tools, the hum of laptops, and Silas’s hands working on damaged frames became a routine within Haven-28
By the end of the fifth day, they had reprogrammed a total of thirty Sentinels. Each one was stripped, rebuilt, and given a new Nano Circuit Board, then loaded with Kai and Mei’s custom firmware.

Distribution was carefully planned. Nine units were stationed at Haven‐28, nine at New Haven‐45, and nine at Freedom Shelter. The remaining three were assigned to guard the cave entrance where the Gene Trader resided.
They had sent the X-01 in that place first and had X-10 and X-11 follow.
Kai insisted on that last placement. "The Trader is too valuable. If locals stumble in and trigger its disappearance, we lose everything. These three will ensure no one interferes."
Indeed, the locals could trigger the mutant traps after all. If enough traps were triggered, the Gene Trader would disappear and no one would be able to stop it.
Because of that, it was better to prevent that from happening.
Soon, Silas looked at the rows of machines with pride.
"This is the last batch... I never thought we’d get this far."
Kai nodded, though his mind was already on the next step.
"This is only the beginning. Once we secure more intact Sentinels, we’ll scale even faster. It means that we have to move the workshop to New Haven-45..."
Of course, the only reason that they weren’t able to continue was due to the lack of Energy Cores.
Well, the Barrier Generator ate up a total of 50 C-Grade and 5 B-Grade Cores after all.
Nonetheless, with the Sentinels deployed, they finally had a moment to breathe.
But for Kai, he was always busy...
Apparently, he needed to visit the Gene Trader’s cave, as he heard the news about the Gene Weapon...
Soon, the store window appeared before him, listing its wares.
His eyes locked on one entry...
[ Gene Weapon (Mid‐Grade) ]
[ Description: A weapon forged with genetic resonance. It greatly synchronizes with the wielder’s Talent, amplifying combat efficiency.
Cost: 30 Survivor Medals ]
Kai exhaled. He only had 34 of them... However, he didn’t have to think too much.
"Thirty medals..." he muttered. "Take it..."
Just like that, he confirmed the purchase. The medals vanished from his inventory, leaving him with only four remaining.
Poverty struck him again, but he didn’t care.
In his hands, a cube materialized... It was smooth, metallic, and seemed to be an ordinary cube...
[ You have obtained a Dormant Gene Weapon. ]
The system prompt followed immediately:
[ Do you wish to awaken it and become its owner? ]
Kai’s grip tightened. There was only one answer.
"Yes," he said firmly.
The cube vibrated, and it started reshaping.
Slowly, it unfolded, reshaping itself into an item...
[ Activating Gene Weapon. ]
[ Connection in progress. ]
[ Synchronizing Spirit Resonance. ]
[ Awakening Sequence Initiated. ]

Just like that, the cube compressed, locking into place around Kai’s forearm. The panels folded neatly, forming a slim gauntlet of dark alloy. It looked plain and functional, built for combat rather than decoration.
[ Gene Weapon Awakened: Strength Gauntlet ]
Kai flexed his fingers, feeling the gauntlet respond instantly. It wasn’t heavy... Instead, it seemed to balance perfectly with his movements, amplifying his strength without resistance.
"I’m pretty close..." Kai muttered.
Finally, he just needed 1 more Gene Weapon to break through his current Level Cap!

chapters.title: Chapter 226: Testing the New Weapon
paragraphs: Kai checked the item once again...
[ Gene Weapon Awakened: Strength Gauntlet ]
[ Grade: Mid ]
[ Type: Resonance Gauntlet ]
[ Effects: +25% Physique Enhancement. Greatly increases grip strength, striking force, and melee damage output. ]
[ Secondary Effect: Brutal Impact - next melee strike deals +50% bonus damage and and knocks enemies backward.
Cooldown: 3 seconds.
Energy Cost: 10 Spirit Energy per activation ]
[ Durability: 100/100 ]

It didn’t have any hidden attributes that required a high-grade Appraisal to be seen, but nonetheless, Kai really liked it. After all, the cooldown of the Brutal Impact was only 3 seconds, and the activation was cheap, only 10 Spirit Energy Points.
Just like that, Kai returned to New Haven‐45 Shelter without purchasing anything more from the Gene Trader.
The cube on his arm had already reshaped into the Strength Gauntlet, and he wanted to see how it performed in real combat.
As soon as he returned, he confirmed that the shelter was busy as always. Survivors moved supplies, repaired defenses, and reinforced walls.
Kai’s first stop was the Barrier Generator. He needed to confirm its progress.
The device sat in the center of the workshop, surrounded by cables and various items.
It was still inactive.
But still, he realized that Victor and the others had managed to repair the Artillery Cannon. The only concern was the fact that they lacked proper ammunition.
For now, the cannons were loaded with stone rounds... They were crude, but better than nothing.
Kai frowned. "I guess Silas has to visit this place soon..." he muttered. "At least the artillery is back online."
He turned away, scanning the yard.
That was when he spotted Alfie, sleeves rolled up, hauling heavy beams to reinforce the outer wall.
He looked really capable as he worked on the walls. Perhaps, the aura of his Gladiator Talent was affecting him...
Kai then had an idea as he approached the guy. "Alfie. You’re still working on the wall?"
Alfie dropped the beam into place and wiped sweat from his forehead.
"Yeah. Barrier Generator isn’t ready... these walls are all we’ve got. We need to get more C-Grade Energy Cores.
Kai nodded. "We need to hunt then... But I came here for another reason. I want to test my gauntlet."
Alfie raised an eyebrow. "Gene Weapon?"
Kai lifted his arm, showing the slim gauntlet of dark alloy. "Strength Gauntlet. Mid‐Grade. I just got it."
Alfie’s eyes widened slightly. "So you finally got another one. Impressive. I’ve been waiting to see what you’d pull from the Trader."
Kai tilted his head. "And you? Still fighting with that sword or axe?"
Alfie smirked. "Not exactly..."
Then, he reached behind him and pulled out a weapon out of nowhere. It was a massive axe. It was not the one being used to cut wood... It was a battleaxe!
Its blade was crimson and looked really heavy!
Indeed, it was his own Gene Weapon!
"This is a Crimson Battleaxe! A mid-grade Gene Weapon!
[ Crimson Battleaxe ]
[ Grade: Mid ]
[ Type: Heavy Weapon ]
[ Effects: +30% Strength Enhancement. Attacks deal cleaving damage in a wide arc. ]
[ Secondary Effect: Blood Rend - strike causes bleeding damage over time.
Cooldown: 10 seconds.
Energy Cost: 12 Spirit Energy per activation ]
[ Durability: 100/100 ]
Kai’s eyes narrowed. "Crimson Battleaxe... That suits you."

Alfie grinned. "It’s heavy, but with my Talent, it feels natural. I’ve been itching to test it properly. Well, it works well against humans, but definitely not what I’ll use against Sentinels... Still, it looks awesome."
Kai laughed at this and raised his gauntlet. "Then let’s spar. I want to see how this gauntlet holds up against your axe."
Alfie’s grin widened. "Finally. I was hoping you’d say that."
They moved to the training yard, a cleared space near the shelter’s perimeter.
Survivors paused their work, curious to see the two fighters.
Word spread quickly... Kai, the Guild Leader, was about to spar with Alfie, the Gladiator.
Kai flexed his gauntlet.
This time, he didn’t plan to use other weapons... Since this was a battle aiming to use their Gene Weapons, they would have maximize its usage.
Alfie rested the Crimson Battleaxe on his shoulder. "Rules?"
Kai thought for a moment. "No killing blows. No Gene Skills beyond weapon activation. Just weapon against weapon. Of course, your passive Gene Skills are all just fine."
If Kai allowed the usage of Active Gene Skill, he’d be able to win easily.
After all, his Spirit Pulse and Specter Step, were already Level 5, and their effects weren’t something he could ignore.
Alfie nodded. "Fair enough. How about this... First to land three decisive hits wins."
Kai raised his gauntlet. "Agreed."
Well, they do not have to heavily injure each other during sparring. Just seeing their moves and the limits of their new Gene Weapons should be more than enough.
Just like that, the sparring began.
Alfie charged first, swinging the Crimson Battleaxe in a vertical slash...
Whoosh~
The weapon whistled through the air as it was heavy and fast.
Kai stepped back, raising his gauntlet to block.
Bang!
The impact rang out, metal against alloy.
Thanks to his Bronze Skin, Kai was able to endure it...
Furthermore, the gauntlet held firm and absorbed the force really well.
Kai countered immediately.
He activated Brutal Impact for 10 Spirit Points!
With the bonus damage, he felt really confident!
His fist shot forward, slamming into Alfie’s chest.
Bang!
The Gladiator staggered back a few steps, as the force drove him off balance. The crowd murmured in surprise.
However, they immediately recalled who he was...
The Gladiator!
Among all the Survivors around, his Strength and Endurance weren’t something they could easily match!
Alfie grinned. "Not bad. That gauntlet packs a punch."
He swung again, this time, he was aiming low.
Kai dodged, rolling to the side, then struck Alfie’s arm with another gauntlet blow.
The alloy connected solidly, but Alfie’s Talent absorbed much of the damage...
"What the..." Kai was shocked. After all, he used all of his strength just now...
He didn’t expect that his Gauntlet wouldn’t be able to knock Alfie down!
However, at this time, Alfie was actually impressed! His Passive Skill called Last Stand, was just triggered!

After all, he used all of his strength just now...
He didn’t expect that his Gauntlet wouldn’t be able to knock Alfie down!
However, at this time, Alfie was actually impressed!
His Passive Skill called Last Stand, was just triggered!

chapters.title: Chapter 227: The Winner and the Dragoons
paragraphs: [ Last Stand (Level 5) ]

[ Description: When Health drops below 50%, the user’s Strength and Endurance increase by 50%. Damage taken is reduced slightly, allowing the user to continue fighting even when heavily injured. This effect lasts until the user’s Health recovers above the threshold. ]
Alfie’s passive skill had triggered the moment Kai’s gauntlet blow connected.
He could actually block that move and avoid getting damaged.
However, he needed to trigger the Last Stand if he wanted to match Kai’s stats!
After all, Kai was already Level 30, and he was missing five more levels to match that.
With that in mind, he took the blow head-on, and soon, Alfie straightened. His breathing became steady, his grip on the Crimson Battleaxe tightened as he prepared to strike.
His body seemed heavier as if his muscles had locked into place.
Kai narrowed his eyes. "So that’s your passive... Last Stand. I heard it from Farrah..."
Alfie grinned. "Exactly. You thought you had me, but this skill makes me harder to knock down. You’ll need more than brute force."
Kai flexed his gauntlet. "Then I’ll just hit harder."
The sparring resumed.
Alfie swung the Crimson Battleaxe in a wide arc, aiming to force Kai back. Kai’s Keen Sense sharpened his perception.
He caught the subtle shift in Alfie’s stance... He saw tense movement of his shoulder muscles, and he moved before the blade could connect. He sidestepped, then drove his gauntlet into Alfie’s ribs.
Bang!
The strike landed cleanly, but Alfie barely flinched. He even smiled at that strike!
His enhanced endurance absorbed the blow.
’Is that chainmail?’Kai wasn’t sure but he knew that he had just hit something.
It wouldn’t even be surprising if Alfie had another Gene Weapon hidden in his body.
"You’re tough... I’ll need to take this more seriously." Kai muttered.
After the cooldown was over, he activated the gauntlet again, channeling Spirit Energy.
This time, he moved faster and his fist slammed into Alfie’s shoulder, the force drove him back several steps. The crowd gasped at the sheer impact, but Alfie steadied himself, refusing to fall.
Alfie laughed. "Fine! That’s two solid hits for you. One more and you win. But I’m not going down that easily."
Alfie knew it himself. The Brutal Impact didn’t just affect his external body. There was a hidden force behind it that was making his internal organs shake.
Still, his Gladiator Talent wasn’t just a name...
It gave him high vitality, endurance, and physique that other would die for...
Soon, he swung the Crimson Battleaxe overhead, aiming for Kai’s head. Kai raised his gauntlet to block.
Bang!
The impact rattled his arm, but his Bronze Skin and Physique boost held firm once again...
He pushed back, forcing Alfie’s weapon aside, then struck again.
Alfie turned, letting Kai’s last strike glance off his armor. "Close... but not enough. My turn."
He shifted his stance and activated the axe’s secondary effect. The Crimson Battleaxe carried extra force and its edge was sharpened by the weapon’s resonance!
"Ha!"
Alfie swung low and this time, it happened so fast that the blade scraped across Kai’s left shoulder.
It was not an injury that Kai would be bothered with since his Bronze Skin would just close it up like always.
However, this time, the strike that cut shallowly into flesh didn’t close. It wasn’t deep, but apparently, it was enough to trigger the weapon’s effect.
Kai frowned as blood began to flow from the wound, staining his shirt.
"That’s Blood Rend," Alfie said with a grin. "Once it cuts, it bleeds."
Kai stepped back, wiping the blood quickly. His Keen Sense kept him alert, tracking Alfie’s movements even as the bleeding drained his stamina.
The Gladiator pressed forward, swinging in horizontal and vertical slashes trying to overwhelm Kai with sheer power.
Kai dodged left, then right, conserving his Spirit Points.
He waited for Brutal Impact’s cooldown to reset.
Alfie pressed harder, and each swing of the Crimson Battleaxe carried the weight of his Gladiator Talent, forcing Kai to stay mobile.
The crowd watched in silence as they didn’t expect this result.
Kai smirked. "Now."
He then charged forward, activating Brutal Impact once more. His fist slammed into Alfie’s chest, harder than before.
The Gladiator stumbled, and his axe dropped slightly as the force drove him back.
Just like that, Alfie dropped to one knee, panting. He couldn’t help but laugh as he knew that he had fought really well against the Guild Leader.
"Three hits. You win."
Kai lowered his gauntlet. "Your axe is powerful..."
Alfie stood, resting the axe on his shoulder again. "True. But in a real fight, I’d use everything... My talent, my full skills. You’d have a harder time then."
Kai smirked. "Then we’ll save that for the battlefield. For now, this sparring was enough."
Alfie let himself drop to the ground, landing on his backside with a heavy exhale.
He leaned against the wall as he retracted his Gene Weapon.
"Whew... That was awesome..." he admitted.
Seeing this, the crowd finally began to disperse. The fight was over, and the entertainment had ended.
Survivors returned to their tasks, though many still talked about what they had just witnessed.
Soon, Kai was about to head back to his quarters to rest when he stopped in his tracks.
Sera and Althea were waiting near the corridor. Both looked healthier than he remembered, their complexions were clear, and they looked more confident...
They had changed into fresh clothes, and judging by the faint scent of soap, they had just finished bathing.
Sera’s ash‐blonde hair and pale brown eyes made her really attractive. Then, Althea’s long dark hair framed her pale skin, giving her a calm but striking presence.
"Kai," Sera said softly, "we need to speak with you. Privately."
Kai blinked, confused. "Privately? Now?"
Althea nodded. "Yes. It’s important."
Though puzzled, Kai agreed.

He led them into his workshop. The room wasn’t much... shelves stacked with loot, crates of supplies, and a desk cluttered with notes. Most of the heavy work was done elsewhere. Kai mainly used this place to organize and plan.
He gestured for them to sit. "Alright. What’s happening?"
The two exchanged a glance before Althea spoke. "We heard something... Victor has already fixed the Dragoons."

chapters.title: Chapter 228: Flying Dragoons
paragraphs: Kai paused for a moment as Althea’s words sank in. "The Dragoons... Victor fixed them?"
Sera nodded. "Yes. Over the past week. He’s been working nonstop. I think it’s because he couldn’t build the Barrier Generator just yet. Wait—you didn’t know? Maybe it’s supposed to be a surprise?"
Althea also realized this, but she could only scratch her head since they had already revealed it to Kai.
"It’s fine..."
Kai nodded as his mind immediately recalled the numerous encounters they’d had with those machines. The Dragoons were unlike the standard Sentinels or Hounds.
They were flying vehicles, similar in shape to oversized jet skis.
Each was designed for speed and mobility, and they could move through the skies very quickly.
The driver resembled a Sentinel, but its lower body was fused into the seat, permanently bound to the machine.
It wasn’t a pilot in the human sense since it was part of the Dragoon itself, a living weapon locked into its vessel.
The design allowed one additional Sentinel to ride on its back, effectively turning the Dragoon into an aerial troop carrier.
Kai remembered vividly how they had been used against them... The A.I. Army deployed them for mobility, surprise attacks, and rapid reinforcement.
A squad of Dragoons could appear out of nowhere, dropping Sentinels directly into the heart of a battle.
Their speed made them difficult to target, and their ability to carry troops gave them devastating reach.
"Interesting... I didn’t know he was working on that." Kai muttered.
After all, he was initially planning to use the Dominion or perhaps Impulse in order to visit Cameron, one of the Human Cities.
However, it seemed that he would be able to use the Dragoons instead, since repairing those two was simply too difficult right now.
"How many?" Kai asked.
"Just one... But he mentioned that he’d be able to fix the others quickly now that he knew how the floating device works. I think he gained some kind of Gene Skill that helped him fix them.
Kai couldn’t help but feel impressed. "So it can be driven by humans now?"

Althea nodded firmly. "Yes. Victor reworked the control systems. He stripped out the Sentinel bindings and replaced them with another device. Anyway, it means a human can sit in the seat and synchronize with the machine."
Sera added, "He said it’s stable. He tested the core himself. The Dragoon responds to human Spirit Energy now, not the A.I. uplink."

Now, this confused Kai even more... This wasn’t just a technology that anyone could easily learn. The fact that Spirit Energy could now be used meant that Victor obtained something incredible. Perhaps his Gene Skill this time was something that could help Survivors connect to the machines through Spirit Energy.
Anyway, he wasn’t sure just yet, but was certainly intrigued.
Kai exhaled slowly.
The implications were enormous.
If they could mobilize many of these modified dragoons, it would be a game changer.
Aerial mobility, rapid deployment, the ability to strike from above... all of it was suddenly within reach.
But it was also dangerous. The Dragoons were fast, but fragile. A single mistake in the air could mean death.
Althea leaned forward...
"That’s why we came to you. We want to pilot them. We don’t want to stay behind anymore. Let us fight in the skies."
Kai studied them both.
Their eyes looked so resolute, and they were definitely not taking no for an answer.
"Fine... I need to see this modified Dragoon first. If it’s too dangerous, we need to add a bit more safety measures before we can use them."
Victor’s workshop was cluttered as always. There were tools scattered across benches, cables snaking across the floor, and half‐finished projects stacked in corners.
Yet Victor himself stood in the middle of it all with a huge smile!
As a matter of fact, he was looking at Kai with a smug face!
"I’m not part of your Sentinel X project," he announced... "but I made my own! Hehehe!"
Kai raised an eyebrow. As expected, Victor really wanted to be part of the Sentinel Reprogramming Project.
"You did well... You can have two Superior Gift Packs and three of the Enhanced Gift Packs of your choice."
Victor spread his arms dramatically. "Yes! Hehe! I will make a list later!"
Then, he turned to look at one of the Dragoons he was currently working on. "You guys can keep your walking tin soldiers. I wanted something thatflies."
Sera tilted her head, smiling faintly. "You sound way too proud of yourself."
"Haha! Of course... I’ll show you."
Victor gestured toward the far end of the workshop.
A tarp was pulled back, revealing the aerodynamic shape of the machine. Its frame resembled an oversized jet ski, streamlined for speed, with stabilizer fins like wings.
The seat was empty now, stripped of its fused Sentinel pilot...
Kai stepped closer, inspecting the modifications. "You actually removed the bindings... and replaced them with a Spirit Energy interface?"
Victor nodded eagerly. "That’s right. It responds to humans now. I tested it myself. It’s stable. In any case, I just asked Miss Mei to fix the software in case it gets connected to Aria."
"So it can fly?" Kai asked.

Victor laughed. "Of course it can fly! But there’s a catch. It needs fuel... in this case, C‐Grade Energy Cores. Five of them will give us about six hours of operation. Not bad for something that used to run entirely on the A.I.’s uplink."
Kai frowned slightly. "Five cores for six hours... That’s expensive."
Victor shrugged. "True, but think of the mobility. Aerial deployment, scouting, rapid reinforcement. We can move faster than the A.I. Army ever expected."
Althea nodded. Her eyes were filled with excitement. "Show us."
Victor grinned like a child about to unveil a toy. "Gladly."
He climbed onto the Dragoon, slotting five glowing C‐Grade cores into the modified chamber.
The machine came alive instantly. Then, a low vibration spread through its frame... It was steady and controlled, as the stabilizers adjusted.
Whom~
It was the sound of energy channels locking into place... Just like that, the cores started feeding power into the propulsion system.
"Watch closely," Victor said as he prepared to take off...

chapters.title: Chapter 229: Test Flight and Visitors
paragraphs: Victor gripped the handlebars and took a deep breath...
As soon as the engine started working, his grin widened.
It was working!
Soon, the Dragoon’s stabilizers locked into place. The hum of the propulsion system grew louder, but it was steady...
"Here we go!" he shouted, his voice echoing through the workshop.
The Dragoon lifted off the ground, hovering for a moment before Victor tilted the handlebars forward. With a sudden burst, the machine shot out of the workshop doors and into the open air!
Kai, Sera, and Althea followed quickly, stepping outside to watch.
"Whoa~"
"That’s fast..."
"Amazing..."
They watched as Dragoon climbed higher... They saw its fins adjusting automatically to balance the weight, and everything looked perfectly fine.
Victor leaned into the handle, and the machine darted across the sky like a hunting bird.
Down below, survivors working in the garden froze, their tools stopped moving as they looked up. Rows of vegetables and fruit trees swayed in the wind as the Dragoon passed overhead.
"Is that... ours?" one of the gardeners whispered, awe in his voice.
On the walls, defenders paused in their patrols.
Some raised their rifles instinctively, then lowered them once they recognized Victor’s figure riding the machine.
"It’s not the A.I. this time," a guard muttered. "It’s one of ours. Finally."
Victor then banked sharply to avoid hitting the wall!
Whoosh~
The Dragoon was cutting across the sky in a wide arc.
The stabilizers were then triggered, keeping the craft steady as he pulled into a dive. He skimmed low over the shelters, the rush of air forcing survivors to shield their faces.
It was such an impressive sight!
Kai narrowed his eyes as he also studied its every movement.
The Dragoon was fast, responsive, and seemed stable enough in the air.
Even without weapons mounted, it was already proving its worth.
Victor pulled up again, climbing higher until he hovered above the walls.
He raised one hand triumphantly, shouting down at the crowd. "Six hours of flight time! That’s what five C‐Grade cores buy us!"
The defenders cheered, some pumping their fists into the air.
Just like that, the sight of a Dragoon’s vessel didn’t bring fear... it actually brought hope.
Victor tested the controls further, moving in tight circles, then accelerating into a straight line before braking suddenly.
The craft obeyed without hesitation, its movements were sharp, and also responsive...
Althea’s eyes gleamed. "It’s perfect. Imagine what we could do with a squad of these."
Sera nodded. "We could strike back easily with this vessel. I want to be part of it!"
Victor finally slowed, guiding the Dragoon back toward the ground.
Thud...
He landed smoothly in front of the workshop...
Whoosh~
Then, the machine settled with a hiss as the propulsion system powered down. He then hopped off, his face flushed with excitement.
"Well?" he asked while spreading his arms. "What do you think?"
Kai shrugged as he voiced out his real thought.
"Yes... It’s impressive. More than I expected. But they’re fragile. We’ll need safety measures before anyone takes it into battle."
Victor smirked. "That’s your part, Guild Leader. I can make it fly... but you’ll decide how we use it."
Around them, survivors were still talking, their voices filled with awe.
The sight of the modified Dragoon was simply too attractive. Kai glanced at Sera and Althea. Their eyes were locked on the machine...
They looked so determined to drive it or be part of the squad that would be built around it.
Kai nodded as he had already seen enough...
"It’s impressive. More than I expected. But tell me, Victor... what else do you need to make more of these?"
Victor’s grin softened into something more serious.
"More modified circuit boards. That’s the real key. Right now, the interface works, but there’s still a risk. We can’t let the A.I. connect to it... If that happens, they could override the pilot."
Sera’s eyes widened. "You mean... they could hijack it?"
Victor nodded grimly. "Exactly..."
"How many do you need?" Kai asked.

Victor rubbed his chin. "As much as you could. To secure a squad, we’ll need dozens. I can work on the hardware since they have to be modified with Spirit Energy channels. Otherwise, the A.I. will find a way in."
Kai nodded. "Alright... Consider it done."

Victor clapped his hands together, excitement bubbling again. "Perfect! With enough boards, I can secure the interface completely. No more risk of A.I. interference. And once that’s done..." He gestured toward the Dragoon, his eyes gleaming. "...we’ll have the skies."
Kai smirked faintly. "Then let’s make sure we’re ready. The next battle won’t wait."
A couple of hours after the test flight had ended, everyone thought that it would just be another normal day, when the alarm suddenly rang across Haven‐45.
Kai’s head turned toward the walls. There was only one ring coming from the bell.
His expression shifted since that meant the visitors weren’t A.I. soldiers or a threat to them.
Still, he moved quickly while Sera and Althea followed at his side. As they reached the gates, Kai saw the line of people outside.
About twenty of them stood in the dust, weary and cautious, but unmistakably human.
The guards had already formed a barrier, rifles were lowered but ready in case needed.
One of them raised a hand to halt the newcomers. "Stop there. Why are you here?"
The group froze. Their leader, a man in his thirties with a patched jacket and tired eyes, stepped forward.
"We’re survivors. Merchants, some of us. We came from shelters farther east... The Grid Region."
Kai studied them carefully. Their origin wasn’t really important right now.
Their clothes were worn, and they all looked skinny. There was no mistaking the desperation in their eyes. They weren’t raiders... they were people seeking refuge.
The guard pressed further. "Which shelters?"
The man swallowed hard. "We were from three different ones in the Grid Region. We couldn’t stay in that region anymore... We’ve been moving for weeks."
Kai’s gaze swept over the group. Some carried packs filled with supplies, others clutched children close. A few had weapons slung over their shoulders, but none raised them.
Althea leaned closer to Kai. "They look exhausted. But that’s a lot of mouths to feed. What do we do, leader?"
Sera added quietly, "If they have information. It might be worth it to accommodate them for some time. We also need to know what’s happening beyond our walls."
Kai nodded at this, but paying with information was not enough... He needed more.
’They’ll be working for us from now on... and those three behind the group. They’re not simple.’

sentences.text: Victor gripped the handlebars and took a deep breath...
As soon as the engine started working, his grin widened.
It was working!
Soon, the Dragoon’s stabilizers locked into place.
The hum of the propulsion system grew louder, but it was steady...
"Here we go!" he shouted, his voice echoing through the workshop.
The Dragoon lifted off the ground, hovering for a moment before Victor tilted the handlebars forward.
With a sudden burst, the machine shot out of the workshop doors and into the open air!
Kai, Sera, and Althea followed quickly, stepping outside to watch.
"Whoa~"
"That’s fast..."
"Amazing..."
They watched as Dragoon climbed higher...
They saw its fins adjusting automatically to balance the weight, and everything looked perfectly fine.
Victor leaned into the handle, and the machine darted across the sky like a hunting bird.
Down below, survivors working in the garden froze, their tools stopped moving as they looked up.
Rows of vegetables and fruit trees swayed in the wind as the Dragoon passed overhead.
"Is that... ours?" one of the gardeners whispered, awe in his voice.
On the walls, defenders paused in their patrols.
Some raised their rifles instinctively, then lowered them once they recognized Victor’s figure riding the machine.
"It’s not the A.I. this time," a guard muttered.
"It’s one of ours.
Finally."
Victor then banked sharply to avoid hitting the wall!
Whoosh~
The Dragoon was cutting across the sky in a wide arc.
The stabilizers were then triggered, keeping the craft steady as he pulled into a dive.
He skimmed low over the shelters, the rush of air forcing survivors to shield their faces.
It was such an impressive sight!
Kai narrowed his eyes as he also studied its every movement.
The Dragoon was fast, responsive, and seemed stable enough in the air.
Even without weapons mounted, it was already proving its worth.
Victor pulled up again, climbing higher until he hovered above the walls.
He raised one hand triumphantly, shouting down at the crowd.
"Six hours of flight time!
That’s what five C‐Grade cores buy us!"
The defenders cheered, some pumping their fists into the air.
Just like that, the sight of a Dragoon’s vessel didn’t bring fear... it actually brought hope.
Victor tested the controls further, moving in tight circles, then accelerating into a straight line before braking suddenly.
The craft obeyed without hesitation, its movements were sharp, and also responsive...
Althea’s eyes gleamed.
"It’s perfect.
Imagine what we could do with a squad of these."
Sera nodded.
"We could strike back easily with this vessel.
I want to be part of it!"
Victor finally slowed, guiding the Dragoon back toward the ground.
Thud...
He landed smoothly in front of the workshop...
Whoosh~
Then, the machine settled with a hiss as the propulsion system powered down.
He then hopped off, his face flushed with excitement.
"Well?" he asked while spreading his arms.
"What do you think?"
Kai shrugged as he voiced out his real thought.
"Yes...
It’s impressive.
More than I expected.
But they’re fragile.
We’ll need safety measures before anyone takes it into battle."
Victor smirked.
"That’s your part, Guild Leader.
I can make it fly... but you’ll decide how we use it."
Around them, survivors were still talking, their voices filled with awe.
The sight of the modified Dragoon was simply too attractive.
Kai glanced at Sera and Althea.
Their eyes were locked on the machine...
They looked so determined to drive it or be part of the squad that would be built around it.
Kai nodded as he had already seen enough...
"It’s impressive.
More than I expected.
But tell me, Victor... what else do you need to make more of these?"
Victor’s grin softened into something more serious.
"More modified circuit boards.
That’s the real key.
Right now, the interface works, but there’s still a risk.
We can’t let the A.I. connect to it...
If that happens, they could override the pilot."
Sera’s eyes widened.
"You mean... they could hijack it?"
Victor nodded grimly.
"Exactly..."

Otherwise, the A.I. will find a way in."

"Alright...

"Perfect!

No more risk of A.I. interference.

chapters.title: Chapter 231: The Rush
paragraphs: Even after Claire’s words, the newcomers couldn’t relax.
Their eyes kept shifting back to the cloaked Sentinels, the faint light coming from the metal beneath their hoods was just impossible to ignore.
Henry couldn’t help but feel a little uneasy...
’She says they’re under control... but how long until the A.I. takes them back? Machines don’t stay loyal. Not in this world.
Nadia’s grip on her pack didn’t ease.

’Survivor Gear or not, those faces are still cold steel. If they’re truly controlled, then this shelter has technology far beyond anything we’ve seen. But if it’s a trick... we’ve walked straight into the lion’s den.’
As expected, they were all still skeptical about the situation.
However, there was still a part of them, hoping that what Claire said was true!
Enzo nodded at Claire to acknowledge her words before he studied the artillery once again.

’That cannon... I’ve only seen weapons like that in the hands of the A.I. Army. If they’ve reprogrammed Sentinels and turned their war machines against the rebellion, then this place is powerful. But if it’s already compromised, we’re nothing but fodder.’
The rest of the group whispered nervously.
Some clutched their children tighter, and others glanced at the gate as it slowly closed behind them.
Thud!
The sound of grinding metal was like a prison door slamming shut.

Henry, Nadia, and Enzo couldn’t help but feel nervous. The three of them were only Level 20 after all. They were also leading a group of people, and they were worried that they had brought these people straight to their doom.
The tension was suffocating. The group stood frozen, caught between hope and terror.
Claire noticed it all...
They still had pale faces and stiff posture even after explaining the situation... The way their eyes lingered on the Sentinels was as if they were expecting them to strike at any moment.
She sighed softly, then stepped closer... This time, her tone was firm but reassuring.

"I know what you’re thinking," she said. "You’ve seen machines tear shelters apart. You’ve seen Sentinels slaughter humans. But here, they’re different. We reprogrammed them. They wear our gear, they fight for us. They’re not disguises or any sort of traps. They’re weapons we’ve taken back. If you’ve seen the Nano Circuit Board and other items looted from them, you should know about this Circuit Board. "
Her words were clear, but the fear didn’t vanish instantly.
Henry, Nadia, and Enzo exchanged glances. They were still wary, but if they wanted to help the group, they had to be the first people to adjust.
In any case, they just checked the Leaderboard, and it was indeed Claire who had reached Rank 5. The only concern now was whether she was the real one or not.
Henry exhaled slowly, lowering his hand from his rifle. Nadia’s grip eased just a little. Enzo also accepted that Claire might be speaking the truth.
Thud!
The gate shut fully behind them, and just like that, they had no other choice but to accept their fate.
The newcomers were quickly ushered into New Haven‐45.

The medic checked them one by one, examining wounds, bruises, and signs of malnutrition. Some of the children were pale and dehydrated, so IV kits from Shane’s Superior Medical Gift Pack were prepared immediately.

The chef also worked just as quickly, boiling water, opening packs, and serving simple meals to ease their hunger. The smell of warm broth and protein concentrate filled the air, and the survivors ate with trembling hands, grateful for even the smallest comfort.
Kai watched from a distance...
Twenty‐two more mouths to feed, twenty‐two more bodies to shelter.
The current space inside New Haven‐45 was already tight. Adding this many people would strain their resources and morale.
But Kai had already thought of a solution...
[ Shelter Gift Pack (Superior) Contents: modular survival pod, weatherproof clothing set, perimeter alarm system set, portable air filtration device, calming incense set, and sleeping bag. ]
After triggering the system, Kai summoned several Shelter Gift Packs.
Soon, Wallace was ordered to distribute them once the newcomers had eaten.
Weatherproof clothing was handed out first... They were thick jackets, durable boots, and layered garments that replaced their ragged, torn clothes.
The survivors changed quickly after washing themselves. They basically shed the filth of weeks on the road.
Next came the modular survival pods. Wallace and a team of locals carried the crates outside the main building, where there was open ground.

Each pod was compact when stored, but once unfolded, it expanded into a sturdy frame with insulated panels. The survivors gathered around, watching nervously at first, then with growing amazement as the pods took shape.
The assembly wasn’t instant.
Wallace directed them step by step... locking the panels into place, securing the supports, and attaching the portable air filtration units as well.
Some of the newcomers joined in, tightening bolts and lifting sections into position.
Soon, the pods clicked together, forming small but secure living spaces.
Children peeked inside, their eyes wide at the sight of clean sleeping bags laid out on the floor. The calming incense was also lit nearby, its faint aroma easing the tension in the air.
Without a doubt, the survivors felt they had a place to rest without fear of Sentinels storming through the night.
Kai also summoned several Food Gift Packs.
[ Food Gift Pack (Superior) Contents: dehydrated meal packs, protein concentrate packs, hydroponic starter kit, fruit juice packs, portable cooking stove with extra fuel. ]

Wallace distributed fruit juice packs to the children, while the adults received their extra dehydrated meals and protein concentrates. Portable stoves were set up near the pods since they couldn’t just rely on the shelter’s chef to eat all the time...
They must learn how to gather food and eat by themselves.
Anyway, the hydroponic starter kits included within the pack were stored for later, to be planted once the group had settled.
Kai observed them quietly.

He also had Status Crystals ready to check their stats, but he decided not to rush. It was their first day inside New Haven‐45, and forcing them into tests would only heighten their anxiety. He would meet everyone else tomorrow, once they had rested and adjusted...
However, as Kai wanted to return to Victor’s workshop, he noticed Claire rushing at him like there was a huge problem!

chapters.title: Chapter 232: New Units and the Monthly
paragraphs: About an hour earlier, Claire had sat with the newcomers while they ate, trying to ease their nerves.
She asked simple questions at first... where they had come from, how long they had been traveling, and what they had seen in the Grid Region.
They weren’t huge secrets, and Claire herself would share information about the Haven Region.

Nadia, still clutching her pack, eventually opened up. "We saw more than Sentinels, Hounds, and Dragoons out there," she said quietly. "There’s another type of machine... one we haven’t seen mentioned in the chat after entering Haven Region."
Henry nodded as he continued with the explanation.
"They’re calledDiggers. Mechanical units built for tunneling. They move underground, using grinder‐like heads to chew through soil, rock, even the hardest concrete..."
Claire paused after hearing this. They were right, this was indeed new information. No one had ever mentioned anything like this in the chat.
Seeing Claire looked surprised, they continued.
"We fought against them and saw them collapse shelters from below. They’re really tricky to deal with. They don’t storm the gates... they come up beneath your feet."

Enzo added grimly, "That’s true... Even a cemented ground would get pierced through by their heads. Ahh... Their heads are shaped like massive drills, and they’re spinning with serrated teeth. When they surface, the ground shakes like there’s an earthquake or something..."

"Just five days ago, we watched one tear through a bunker wall like it was paper. Once they breach, they release smaller units within their compartments, mostly Bomber Swarmers, directly inside. It’s not a normal siege. It’s infiltration."
Claire’s eyes widened.Diggers that release Bomber Swarmers...
"Is this a D-Rank? No... C-Rank Units?"

Nadia nodded. "Yes... All of them are C-Ranks at the very least... We saw them coordinating with Sentinels. They’d tunnel beneath, then emerge in sync with surface attacks. That’s how Grid shelters fell so quickly. Defenses meant nothing when the enemy came from below."
Henry’s jaw tightened. "We lost so many shelters to them. The defenders thought they were safe behind walls and artillery. But the Diggers undermined everything. Once they surfaced, chaos followed."

Enzo’s voice dropped. "And here’s the worst part. On our way here, we noticed signs. There were mall protrusions in the ground. At first, we thought they were debris or old pipes. But the patterns were too familiar. The soil was disturbed in ways we’d seen before. I’m telling you... The Diggers are already here, in the Haven Region. They’re scouting and probably waiting."
Nadia’s hands trembled slightly as she spoke. "If they’re here, then Haven‐45 isn’t safe. None of the shelters are. We might be expecting them soon."
The group around them fell silent, listening with pale faces.
The idea of machines burrowing beneath their feet was terrifying.
Walls, gates, trip wires, pit traps, artillery... They were all useless if the ground itself betrayed them.
Claire forced herself to stay calm, but she was already thinking what they could do against the Diggers.

’If what they’re saying is true, then every defense we’ve built could be compromised. Well, the Sentinels that got reprogrammed will be useful to tank them at the very least... However, the artillery we salvaged wouldn’t matter if the enemy came from below.’
She asked carefully, "Did you see how they detect targets? Do they move randomly, or do they track survivors?"
Well, the Diggers must have a method for finding their targets. She was curious if the targets were detected through heat signatures, trackers, or tagged by Sentinels first.

Henry shook his head. "We couldn’t figure it out. Sometimes they surfaced near large groups, sometimes near shelters. But they never wasted effort. Every time they appeared, it was coordinated. My guess? They’re guided by the A.I.’s network, scanning for concentrations of human activity. Not sure..."
Enzo added, "And once they lock onto a location, they don’t stop. They’ll grind through anything. Steel, stone, reinforced barriers... nothing holds them back."
Nadia’s voice was quiet but firm. "We need to prepare. If those protrusions we saw are signs of Diggers, then Haven‐45 could be next. You should warn Kai. He needs to know before it’s too late."
Claire nodded... She realized this wasn’t a simple matter. They were right, Kai needed to learn all of this.
These three had lived through it, seen shelters collapse from beneath. Their words carried the weight of survivors who had lost everything.
That was why, an hour later, after she gathered all the information she needed from them and even brought a sketch of the Digger, she rushed to Kai...
Claire laid the rough sketch of the Digger unit on the table.
The jagged drill‐like head, serrated teeth, and reinforced chassis were unmistakable.
"This is what they saw in the Grid Region," she explained. "They tunnel beneath shelters, breach walls, and release Bomber Swarmers inside. If they’re already scouting here, Haven‐45 could be next."
Kai studied the drawing in silence. This was indeed a huge deal.
He nodded slowly. "If they’re guided by the A.I. network, then brute defenses won’t be enough. We’ll need some countermeasures."
He tapped the sketch with his finger. "First, the disruptor field units. If these things rely on signals to coordinate, we’ll deploy more portable disruptor fields around the perimeter."

His Stealth Gift Pack has them... He believed that if they positioned those devices deeper underground and also in various areas outside their shelter, it would assist them in slowing down the enemies.
"Maybe they’ll scramble transmissions and weaken the Diggers’ ability to sync with surface units."
After all, if they were using the Sentinels to coordinate their siege, it would be a good method to counter that.
Claire agreed. "That could buy us time. But if they somehow surface inside the walls..."

Kai’s eyes narrowed. "Then we just hit them hard. More grenade launchers, fragmentation rounds. We will distribute the launchers from my Weapon Gift Pack. If a Digger breaches, we saturate the area before the swarmers spread."
He paused, considering the survivors. "We’ll also need to boost our fighters. Gene stimulant injectors from the Water Gift Pack... They will be rationed to everyone."
Claire nodded, already picturing the distribution.
Thankfully, Kai’s Infinite Gift Pack was still reliable...
Then, on the next day, as Kai distributed more Gene Stimulants, he suddenly got a message!
[ Congratulations! Monthly Rankings Concluded! ]

That was why, an hour later, after she gathered all the information she needed from them and even brought a sketch of the Digger, she rushed to Kai...
Claire laid the rough sketch of the Digger unit on the table.
The jagged drill‐like head, serrated teeth, and reinforced chassis were unmistakable.
"This is what they saw in the Grid Region," she explained.
"They tunnel beneath shelters, breach walls, and release Bomber Swarmers inside.
If they’re already scouting here, Haven‐45 could be next."
Kai studied the drawing in silence.
This was indeed a huge deal.
He nodded slowly.
"If they’re guided by the A.I. network, then brute defenses won’t be enough.
We’ll need some countermeasures."
He tapped the sketch with his finger.
"First, the disruptor field units.
If these things rely on signals to coordinate, we’ll deploy more portable disruptor fields around the perimeter."
His Stealth Gift Pack has them...
He believed that if they positioned those devices deeper underground and also in various areas outside their shelter, it would assist them in slowing down the enemies.
"Maybe they’ll scramble transmissions and weaken the Diggers’ ability to sync with surface units."
After all, if they were using the Sentinels to coordinate their siege, it would be a good method to counter that.
Claire agreed.
"That could buy us time.
But if they somehow surface inside the walls..."
Kai’s eyes narrowed.
"Then we just hit them hard.
More grenade launchers, fragmentation rounds.
We will distribute the launchers from my Weapon Gift Pack.
If a Digger breaches, we saturate the area before the swarmers spread."
He paused, considering the survivors.
"We’ll also need to boost our fighters.
Gene stimulant injectors from the Water Gift Pack...
They will be rationed to everyone."
Claire nodded, already picturing the distribution.
Thankfully, Kai’s Infinite Gift Pack was still reliable...
Then, on the next day, as Kai distributed more Gene Stimulants, he suddenly got a message!
[ Congratulations!
Monthly Rankings Concluded! ]

chapters.title: Chapter 233: The Rewards and the Gene Skill
paragraphs: [ Congratulations! Monthly Rankings Concluded! ]
[ Survivor Leaderboard - Cycle 2 Complete ]
[ Requirement: Level 10+ ]
[ All calculations finalized. Rewards are now being distributed. ]
[ Congratulations, Survivor Kai! ]
[ You have achieved Rank 1 in the Monthly Leaderboard. ]
[ Special Rewards have been granted. ]
"Whoa... Another month had passed, huh..." Kai muttered as he didn’t expect to still be the rank 1 even after being stuck at Level 30.
’I guess it’s because I’m the first to reach Level 30...’
At this time, there were already several survivors who had reached Level 30. Even Claire herself was already Level 30 like him after the last Global Event.
It wouldn’t be surprising if he checked the Guild Leaderboard now and found other Guilds around.

However, the reason he and many others were stuck at this level was due to the huge requirement of absorbing 10 B-Grade Energy Cores, getting 5 Gene Skills at Level 5, and lastly, binding 3 Gene Weapons!
’Let’s see what rewards I will get this time...’
Kai mused as he recalled that he got the title Strongest One before basically increasing his base attributes. It was only an additional 5%, but that was a huge deal at this early stage.
There was also the Talent Upgrade Crystal, the Supply Crate, and the Gene Skill Crystal that he could use or even sell if he wanted to...
[ Rank 1 Special Rewards ]
[ Title Enhancement: Strongest One
Effect: Increases all base attributes (Strength, Agility, Endurance, Perception) by +10%. Grants passive intimidation effect against lower-level human enemies. ]
"Ahhh..."
Kai clenched his fist as he felt the surge of power through his body.
"Ten percent... That’s double the boost from before."
The intimidation effect was also always welcome and he couldn’t help but feel curious how intimidation really works.
In any case, he only knew how lower‐ranked survivors would hesitate under his presence, but other than that, he wasn’t really sure.
Anyway, his gaze shifted to the next reward. This time, he really froze as he didn’t expect something like this to appear.
[ Item Acquired: Skill Fusion Crystal x1
Effect: Allows fusion of two or more existing Gene Skills into a new hybrid skill. Higher compatibility between fused skills produces stronger results. Single‐use, bound to the player. ]
"Fusion...?" He muttered, almost disbelieving.

’If I fuse two Gene Skills... what kind of hybrid could I create?’He thought of his Bronze Skin, his Spirit Pulse, and all other skills... The possibilities were huge. However, he had to consider finding compatible skills to fuse to get a better result.
"This is incredible..." Kai muttered.
He then exhaled slowly, forcing himself to stay calm.
"But it’s single‐use. I can’t waste it. I’ll need to study compatibility or synergy, and choose carefully. The wrong fusion could ruin everything."
Then, after checking the rest of the rewards, he confirmed that they were all just quite normal.
[ Reputation Points +20 ]
[ Note: Reputation Store will activate upon reaching Level 31. Reputation Points can be exchanged for rare items, unique skills, or certain privileges. Current Balance: 190 Points. ]
[ Bonus Reward: ]
[ Survival Supply Crate (x5)
Contents: Randomized consumables, weapon parts, and enhancement materials.
Guaranteed: 1 Rare Weapon Component and 1 Advanced Healing Serum. ]
[ Specialized Gene Skill Crystal (High‐Grade) x1 ]
[ Prototype Gene Weapon Core x1
Effect: Can be bound to a Gene Weapon to unlock hidden attributes or evolve it into a higher tier. ]
[ Leaderboard Summary - Cycle 2 ]
Rank 1: Kai - Level 30
Rank 2: Mei - Level 30
Rank 3: Renji - Level 30
Top 20 Survivors have received Basic Rewards.
[ Reminder: Cycle 3 begins immediately. Rankings reset. ]
[ Next distribution in 30 days. ]
Kai was so excited to open his rewards. But for now, he went into the warehouse and opened one of the crates!
[ Do you want to open a Survival Supply Crate? ]
Just like that, the faint glow of the System appeared as the contents materialized...
There were weapon components, enhancement materials, and a neatly sealed vial of Advanced Healing Serum.
[ Survival Supply Crate Opened!
You have received
Plasma Power Cell x1, Advanced Recovery Serum x1, Dried Meat Pack x10, Bottled Water x10
First Aid Kit x1, Portable Cooking Pot x1, Rice Sack (5kg) x1 ]
He smirked. "Not bad... everything here is useful."
Satisfied, he opened the remaining four crates one by one.
[ Survival Supply Crate Opened!
You have received
Plasma Power Cell x1, Advanced Recovery Serum x1, Soap & Disinfectant Pack x3, Bottled Water x10, Portable Lantern x1, First Aid Kit x1, Dried Fish Pack x5, Sewing Kit x2 ]
As expected, each crate had randomized items except for the guaranteed component of a rare weapon and the recovery serum.
’Still... I’m lucky to get two power cells in a row...’
After taking them all out in the warehouse, Althea arrived soon after...
She inspected the crates and smiled. "I’ll arrange them later..."
Kai gave her a brief nod. "Good..."
As he took the serums and a few items from the crates, he finally left the warehouse. But just outside the building, he noticed Wallace, Victor, and several others arriving.
They were already discussing the crates they were about to open. Well, they were also planning how to unload and catalog the crates for distribution.
Kai didn’t linger... he trusted them to handle the details.
Back in his room, Kai sat down and pulled out the Specialized Gene Skill Crystal (High Grade). The faint pulse of energy inside the crystal was mesmerizing, like a living flame trapped in glass.
He held it tightly while closing his eyes.
"Alright... let’s see what you’ve got for me."
Soon, he received the activation confirmation, and after agreeing to it, the System responded immediately...
[ Specialized Gene Skill Crystal Activated ]
[ Searching for compatible Gene Skill pathways... ]
[ Randomized outcome based on current affinity and talent resonance. ]
Kai exhaled, almost like a prayer. "Give me something good..."
Soon, the crystal dissolved into pure light, flooding his body with warmth.
Just like that, the System gave him a new skill!
’Please be an Active Gene Skill... No more Passive please! Active Skills are the best!’
[ New Gene Skill Acquired! ]

chapters.title: Chapter 234: New Gene Skill and the Weapon
paragraphs: [ New Gene Skill Acquired! ]
[ Skill: Beast Arm (Level 0) ]
[ Type: Active ]
[ Description: Temporarily transforms the user’s right arm into a beast‐like appendage, increasing raw strength and impact force.
Strikes deal +25% bonus damage and can fracture defensive barriers.
Duration: 20 seconds.
Cooldown: 120 seconds. ]
[ Activation Cost: 70 SP ]
[ Note: Transformation places strain on the body. Overuse may cause fatigue or minor tissue damage. ]
Kai stared at his right arm as the faint glow faded.
For a brief instant, he had seen claws forming, his forearm swelling with unnatural power. He flexed his hand, feeling the lingering heaviness as it returned to normal like nothing really happened.
"...Beast Arm," he muttered. "Interesting."

He tested a punch against the wall, stopping short before impact. Even without activating it, he could sense the potential... a skill designed to break through armor, crush obstacles, and overpower enemies in close combat.
Furthermore, it wasn’t really that limiting to use. The duration was 20 seconds, and the cooldown of 2 minutes wasn’t that bad considering the cost of activation.
Then, he also learned something...
"This... stacks perfectly with Bronze Skin," Kai realized.
"It covered both defense and offense... Spirit Pulse for ranged bursts, Specter Step for mobility, and now Beast Arm for brute force."
Kai exhaled with a grin tugging at his lips.
"The System really wants me to fight head‐on."
At this time, just as Kai was about to relax, another notification appeared before his eyes.
Ding!
[ Compatibility Detected! ]
[ Passive Skill: Bio‐Adaptive Constitution (Level 5) ]
[ Active Skill: Beast Arm (Level 0) ]
[ Status: High Compatibility Confirmed ]
"What? There’s something like this?" Kai muttered, pausing as he read the new message.

It was surprising, but the more he thought about it, the more sense it made. This was the first time he had obtained a skill that directly transformed his body. Naturally, Bio‐Adaptive Constitution would respond to such a change.

The passive skill wasn’t just about resisting rejection from synthetic modifications — it also triggered whenever his physiology underwent transformation. In this case, it was stabilizing Beast Arm, ensuring his body could handle the strain without tearing itself apart.
In any case, the notification didn’t end just yet.
[ Effect Integration: ]
- Bio‐Adaptive Constitution stabilizes Beast Arm’s transformation, reducing strain on muscle tissue and preventing rejection of foreign augmentation.
- Fatigue penalty reduced by 100%.
- Transformation duration extended from 20 seconds to 45 seconds.
- Damage bonus increased from +25% to +35%.
- Barrier Fracture chance improved: +15% effectiveness against hardened defenses.
- Recovery time shortened: Cooldown reduced from 120 seconds to 90 seconds.
[ Additional Note: ]
[ Due to seamless integration, Beast Arm’s growth potential has increased. Future leveling will unlock advanced mutations (multi‐limb reinforcement, claw extension, or dual‐arm transformation). ]
Kai blinked at the sight of it. He was stunned. "It... boosted the skill?"

He flexed his right arm again, recalling the heaviness he had felt earlier. Now, the System confirmed it wasn’t just brute force... his body had adapted instantly, thanks to Bio‐Adaptive Constitution.
"This is insane," he muttered.
"My constitution actually canceled the drawbacks of the Beast Arm. Instead of strain, I get more power, longer duration, and faster recovery."
Finally, Kai opened his inventory, and this time, he focused on the icon of a purple crystal.
[ Item: Skill Fusion Crystal ]
[ Effect: Allows fusion of two or more Gene Skills into a new hybrid skill. Higher compatibility produces stronger results. Single-use, bound to the player. ]
He materialized it into his hand. At first glance, it looked like nothing more than an ordinary stone. It was dull, smooth, and unimpressive. But the moment he held it, the System reacted.
Ding!
[ Skill Fusion Crystal Activated ]
[ Eligible Gene Skills Detected ]
[ Active Skills: Spirit Pulse Lv5, Specter Step Lv5, Fast Appraisal Lv5, Beast Arm Lv0 ]
[ Passive Skills: Keen Sense Lv5, Bio‐Adaptive Constitution Lv5, Battle Trance Lv5, Bronze Skin Lv5 ]
[ Instruction: Select up to 5 Gene Skills to fuse together. ]
[ Note: Minimum requirement is 2 Gene Skills. Fusion will proceed with chosen skills. ]
[ Warning: The more skills selected, the higher the risk of failure or unstable results unless compatibility is high. ]
[ Recommendation: Choose carefully. Fusion outcomes are permanent. ]
Kai frowned as he read the notification. "Up to five skills... but that’s insane. If compatibility isn’t perfect, I could ruin everything."
He thought of Spirit Pulse and Specter Step... both seemed to be spirit‐based, both offensive and evasive. They might fuse well. But adding Beast Arm or Bronze Skin into the mix? That was riskier.
"No... not yet," Kai muttered. He canceled the process, and soon the crystal dimmed back into in his hands.
"I’ll study compatibility first. I can’t waste this."
Just like that, he stored it back in his inventory.
His gaze shifted to another item in his inventory... one he had nearly forgotten.
[ Prototype Gene Weapon Core x1 ]
[ Effect: Can be bound to a Gene Weapon to unlock hidden attributes or evolve it into a higher tier. ]
Kai’s lips tightened. He currently had two mid‐grade Gene Weapons.

He needed one more to break through the requirement for his level cap. But Gene Weapons were permanent... once bound, there was no turning back. Binding a low‐grade weapon would be a mistake he might regret forever.
Still... with the Prototype Core, he could change that. He could evolve a low‐grade weapon into something greater.
Kai reached into his inventory and pulled out a black cube... the dormant form of his low‐grade Gene Weapon. It had been sitting there for weeks, untouched.
"Alright... let’s see what you can become."
Without any more hesitation, he activated the cube.
[ Dormant Gene Weapon Detected ]
[ Do you wish to awaken it and become its owner? ]
"Yes," he said firmly.
Just like that, the cube vibrated, and it started reshaping.
Slowly, it unfolded, reshaping itself into an item...
[ Activating Gene Weapon. ]
[ Connection in progress. ]
[ Synchronizing Spirit Resonance. ]
[ Awakening Sequence Initiated. ]
The cube unfolded, and its segments elongated instead of compressing.
Soon, metallic shafts extended outward... The core stretched into a long pole, while the tip sharpened into a spearhead of dark alloy.
Just like that, the weapon stabilized... It was a lance, built for piercing through armor and striking at range.
[ Gene Weapon Awakened: War Lance ]

chapters.title: Chapter 235: Breakthrough, Rewards, and the Store
paragraphs: [ Gene Weapon Awakened: War Lance ]
[ Grade: Low ]
[ Type: Piercing Lance ]
[ Effects: +12% Piercing Damage. Attacks ignore 10% of the enemy defense. Effective against armored targets. ]

[ Secondary Effect: Perfect Thrust - repeated strikes on the same point increase penetration chance. After three consecutive hits on the same spot, the next thrust guarantees armor break. Cooldown: 3 second.
Activation Cost: 12 Spirit Energy per activation ]
[ Durability: 50/50 ]
Kai gripped the lance tightly, testing its balance. The weapon felt heavier than a sword... But its reach and piercing power were undeniable.
"A lance... finally, something for range and armor penetration," he muttered. "But low‐grade... it won’t be enough."
His eyes shifted to the glowing crystal in his inventory.
[ Prototype Gene Weapon Core x1 ]
[ Effect: Can be bound to a Gene Weapon to unlock hidden attributes or evolve it into a higher tier. ]
With the War Lance in his right hand, he activated the Core and the System reacted instantly.
[ Prototype Core Detected. Integration possible. ]
[ Do you wish to evolve War Lance? ]
"Yes," Kai replied without hesitation.

Just like that, the lance vibrated violently, its alloy frame started resonating with the Core’s energy. Soon, lines of light surged across the shaft, and the spearhead glowed as the weapon’s structure shifted.
[ Upgrade in Progress... ]
[ Bound Complete! ]
As soon as Kai saw this, he knew that it was time to level up! Finally, 3 decent Gene Weapons!
[ Gene Weapon Evolved: War Lance ]
[ Grade: Mid ]
[ Type: Piercing Lance ]
[ Effects: +30% Piercing Damage. Attacks ignore 20% of enemy defense. Effective against armored and shielded targets. ]

[ Secondary Effect: Perfect Thrust - repeated strikes on the same point increase penetration chance. After three consecutive hits on the same spot, the next thrust guarantees armor break. Cooldown: 1 second.
Activation Cost: 15 Spirit Energy per activation ]
[ Durability: 100/100 ]
Kai’s eyes widened as he studied the stats. "Mid‐grade... This is awesome."
He spun the lance once, then twice... Until he started practicing with it for a few more minutes.
The weapon wasn’t just a polearm anymore... it was an extension of his arm, capable of piercing armor up close and striking enemies from a distance!
"This is just too good." Kai muttered as he knew how great it was.
The moment the War Lance stabilized in his grip, Kai saw another set of notifications!
A cascade of light filled his vision!
[ Breakthrough Requirement Completed ]
[ Quest: Strengthen Your Foundation
- Five Gene Skills upgraded to Level 5
- Ten B‐Grade Energy Cores absorbed
- Three Gene Weapons bound to your body
Status: All conditions fulfilled. Restriction lifted. ]
Kai smiled. This was what he was waiting for. He really felt excited as the next message appeared.
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ Level: 31 ]
[ Health Points +500 ]
[ Spirit Points +50 ]
[ Physique Rating has greatly improved! ]

chapters.title: Chapter 236: The Store and the Potions
paragraphs: Kai scrolled further down the list, and he couldn’t help but smile after seeing the next entry in the list.
[ High‐Grade EMP Grenade ] [ 3/3 ]
[ Cost: 30 RP ]
[ Effect: Emits a concentrated electromagnetic pulse on detonation. Immediately disables drones, turrets, and mechanical units within a 100‐meter radius. Effective even against shielded constructs. ]
Kai remembered that the Gene Traders were selling some EMP Grenades for 10,000 Experience Points. Kai purchased a couple of them before, since he was level-capped anyway.
This time, however, a stronger version of it was being sold for a steep price.
Reputation Points weren’t easy to obtain. Using thirty of them for a single-use grenade was a bit too much in Kai’s opinion.
Of course, the range was definitely great, but in the end, he had other items he could choose to use in case of emergency.
For now, Kai turned his attention elsewhere.
Well, the next item intrigued him a lot.
[ Neural Gear Interface ] [ 1/1 ]
[ Cost: 200 RP ]
[ Effect: A device that allows the wearer to enter the virtual world through installed applications. Connection is untraceable and immune to hacking attempts. ]
Kai didn’t know what to say as he saw the icon of the Neural Gear.
"Virtual World? What kind? Why would I even need to enter it?" Kai muttered, clearly confused.
The System hinted that certain applications were required before entry was possible.
’Applications, huh... Where am I supposed to get them? Are they sold here in the Reputation Store? Or... maybe in the Human Cities?’
This guess wasn’t just something he came up with out of nowhere.
He had been thinking what kind of things he’d see in a human city that wasn’t brought down by the A.I. Army yet.
There, he was actually expecting too see more advanced tech that even Aria, the A.I. Rebel, couldn’t actually control.
Perhaps, there was actually a virtual world controlled by these high-level Survivors.
After calming down, Kai finally checked the fourth item...
[ Hair Growth Serum ] [ 5/5 ]
[ Cost: 5 RP ]
[ Effect: Guaranteed 100% success rate. Restores natural hair growth regardless of age, genetics, or damage. Permanent effect. ]
"Ugh~"
Kai chuckled while shaking his head. "Seriously? In the middle of an apocalypse, the System’s selling miracle hair cream? ...Still, I bet half the survivors would kill for this. Morale matters too."
Finally, the fifth item appeared. On its icon, it shows a vial glowing faintly with green.
[ Hundred Poison Immunity Serum ] [ 2/2 ]
[ Cost: 50 RP ]
[ Effect: Grants permanent immunity to hundred known toxins, venoms, and chemical poisons. Effective against both natural and synthetic compounds. ]
Kai gently nodded as he saw the serum.
This was definitely an interesting item... After all, even the food they eat could contain poison at some point. This Serum might also help them avoid contracting disease.
"This is nice... But for 50 Reputation Points? Even if I have 2 Vouchers that gives 50% discount, I don’t think this a priority..."
In any case, it didn’t change the fact that he was excited about these store items.
Each item wasn’t just rare... they were strange and undeniably unique!
Still, Kai decided not to purchase anything just yet.
With only 200 Reputation Points and two vouchers, he knew he had to be careful.
The store’s items were tempting, but the cost was steep, and his resources were limited. For now, patience was the smarter choice.
The following day, Victor approached him with a grin that Kai hadn’t seen in a long time.

"Good news," Victor announced. "I managed to repair two more Dragoons. That makes three modified units ready for deployment. They can operate for six hours straight using five C‐Grade Energy Cores as their power source."
Kai’s eyes widened. It seemed that Victor had also gained a lot after reaching Level 30 through the usage of Alpha Gene Enhancement Serums.
In any case, three Dragoons meant a lot for them... They could be used for mobility, air support, and a tactical edge against the A.I. Army. But the mention of the cores made him pause.
Originally, Kai had planned to absorb those C‐Grade Cores in his Inventory by himself. Each one would have given him valuable experience points, a direct boost to his growth.
But now, they were needed as batteries for the Dragoons... He even had to save more for the Barrier Generator that would be available soon.
Right now, the choice was clear... Their survival and strategy outweighed personal gain.
Still, as he reached this thought, he recalled his Inventory!
He recalled the Instant Experience Potions he had stockpiled.
’Right... I almost forgot about them.’
He had twenty vials in total, over the past month. Back then, the level cap had made them useless. But now, with the restriction lifted, they were exactly what he needed.
Kai then quickly went to his safe space and opened his inventory. He carefully withdrew all of the blue vials. They looked ordinary, almost like a juice drink, but only 10mL in size.
’Let’s go...’
He uncorked the first vial and drank.
Gulp~
A rush of energy surged through him instantly.
[ You have received 5,000 Experience Points. ]
Kai smirked. "Just as expected."
One after another, he consumed the potions.
The experience points continued stacking higher and higher...
By the time he finished the fifth vial, the System chimed again.
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ Level: 32 ]
[ Health Points +10 ]
[ Spirit Points +2 ]
[ Physique Rating has slightly improved! ]
’Seriously... I need 25,000 points to level up?’
That was an enormous amount of experience points!
Still, Kai recalled that he had needed 50,000 Experience Points just to reach the limit of Level 30.
At that time, when he finally hit the cap, only then did the System reveal what conditions he had to fulfill in order to break through the bottleneck.
Just like that, Kai continued consuming the fifteen more vials and reached level 35!
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ Level: 35 ]
[ Health Points +100 ]
[ Spirit Points +5 ]
[ Physique Rating has slightly improved! ]
[ Inventory Slots Expanded: +1 ]
[ Skill Point +1 ]
[ Reputation Point +1 ]
