chapters.title: Chapter 237: The Division and the Team
paragraphs: Kai made a quick look on his current stat...
[ Name: Kai ]
[ Title: Expert Survivor, Trailblazer, Stronghold Defender, Guardian, Strongest One ]
[ Guild: Codebreakers ]
[ Level: 35 ]
[ Physique Rating: C+ ]
[ Talent: Infinite Gift Pack (SSS) ]
[ Active Skills: Spirit Pulse Lv5, Specter Step Lv5, Fast Appraisal Lv5, Beast Arm Lv0 ]
[ Passive Skills: Keen Sense Lv5, Bio Adaptive Constitution Lv5, Battle Trance Lv5, Bronze Skin Lv5 ]
[ Skill Points: 11 ]
[ Reputation Points: 201 ]
[ Inventory Slots: 9 ]
Seeing that his Beast Arm was the only one that was level zero, he used up his five Skill Points and pushed it to Level 5 as well.
After all of this, Kai finally stepped into Victor’s workshop...
The familiar scent of oil and scorched alloy filled the air. He planned to test the new, modified Dragoons that Victor had just made.
However, as soon as he got closer, there was already a crowd gathering outside to check Victor’s creations.
Mei and Wallace were already mounted on one of the newly repaired Dragoons. The simple jet‐ski-like frame hovered a few feet above the ground...
Indeed, outside, in the open yard, two of the modified Dragoons hovered a few feet above the ground.
Mei sat in the pilot’s seat, gripping the handlebars nervously...
"Ease up! Don’t fight it... let the stabilizers do the work!" Victor reminded.
The vessel wobbled as she tilted too sharply, the stabilizers were fighting to keep her steady.
Hearing Victor’s reminder, she gritted her teeth, adjusting her grip, while the Dragoon swayed left and right before finally leveling out.
On another Dragoon, Wallace was testing his own skills.
His approach was more aggressive, pushing the craft forward in sudden bursts. The machine rocked, nearly scraping the workshop wall, before he corrected the angle.
He laughed nervously, muttering, "Alright... not as easy as it looks."
Kai wryly smiled, watching them both. Their movements were clumsy, but the machines were responsive.
Victor’s modifications had worked... the Dragoons were stable, just waiting for their riders to learn the rhythm.

Minutes passed, and both Mei and Wallace began to improve. Mei’s Dragoon glided smoothly across the yard, banking in wide curves. Wallace also managed a sharp turn without losing control... As expected, his confidence grew with each maneuver.
Victor grinned beside Kai. "See? They’ll get the hang of it. The systems are solid."
Kai nodded. "Not bad. It’s rough at first, but once you trust the stabilizers, I guess it feels natural."
Finally, it was his turn. He climbed into the third Dragoon, settling into the seat.
The handlebars felt firm and the controls felt responsive. With a tilt forward, the craft surged into the air, pressing him down with sudden force.
’Whoa~’
The wind whipped against his face as he climbed higher.
Kai banked left, then right, testing the stabilizers.
Whoosh~ Whoosh~
The Dragoon obeyed flawlessly, cutting through the air seamlessly.
He skimmed low over the compound, then pulled up into a hover above the walls.
"Responsive," Kai muttered, pushing the craft harder. He dove, pulled into tight turns, and stopped abruptly mid‐air.
The Dragoon handled every maneuver smoothly, Victor’s rework proving its worth.
’This is an incredible work... I have to reward him again.’
Victor was a talent he couldn’t lose. If he needed to bribe him with some of the Superior Gift Packs, he wouldn’t mind it at all.
Minutes passed, and Kai felt the rhythm of the machine...
"I guess having a higher level helped me easily learn how to pilot it." Kai muttered.
Soon, he landed smoothly and dismounted with a satisfied look on his face.
"How was it?" Victor asked.
"It’s stable. More than I expected. With three of these, we can move fast..."
Victor nodded. "So? What’s the plan?"
He already had an answer in his mind, but he wanted to hear it from Kai.
Kai smiled as he looked toward the horizon.
"It’s time. We’ll use the Dragoons to reach Cameron. The Human City might hold the tech we need... and the answers we’ve been waiting for."
Mei and Wallace exchanged excited glances...
The decision was made. The Codebreakers were no longer bound to three shelters... Their path to Cameron had just opened.
Just like that, Kai decided to bring a total of five people with him to Cameron.
Although the invitation from Cornelio Aries was for Kai alone, the man had also mentioned that Level 30 Survivors are all welcome in the city...
With that in mind, he chose Mei, Claire, Alfie, Farrah, and Ralph...
Kai would ride with Mei, Claire with Alfie, and Ralph with Farrah on the last modified Dragoon.
Of course, Kai knew that leaving for Cameron couldn’t be rushed. Even with three Dragoons ready, the shelters had to be secured first.
The twenty‐two newcomers who had arrived days earlier were still settling in.

Kai had already decided they couldn’t all remain in one place. If they were scattered across the three shelters, even if some had hidden intentions, they wouldn’t be able to cause significant trouble.
"Divide them," Kai ordered during the meeting with the other important members of his shelter.
"Seven to Shelter‐28, eight to Freedom Shelter, and the rest here in New Haven‐45. That way, we balance the risk and strengthen each base."
Before leaving, Kai assigned the managers...
Victor and Wallace were assigned to oversee New Haven‐45. Their mechanical expertise and leadership would keep the heart of the Codebreakers strong.

Sera, alongside his Sentinel Atom, would take charge of Haven‐28. Silas was already producing modified Sentinels there, and Sera’s cautious nature made him the right choice to guard against any sabotage.
Althea and Aurora were tasked with Freedom Shelter. The crops there had finally begun to flourish, and protecting the food supply was critical.
"That field is our lifeline," Kai reminded them. "Guard it as if it were the walls themselves."
With the preparations underway, Kai turned his attention to the newcomers.
Among them, three stood out... Henry, Nadia, and Enzo.
He knew they were also Foreign Survivors, transmigrated into this world, each with skills and talents that could prove invaluable.
’I guess it’s time to complete that Guild Mission...’
Kai found Henry near the training yard, his rifle slung across his back. The man’s posture was disciplined, and his eyes swept across every corner as though he expected an ambush at any moment.
He looked interesting, but Kai was intrigued upon seeing the man’s eyes...
"Is that an Ocular Replacement Implant?" Kai asked.
Henry froze, stunned by the question.

Don’t fight it... let the stabilizers do the work!" Victor reminded.
The vessel wobbled as she tilted too sharply, the stabilizers were fighting to keep her steady.
Hearing Victor’s reminder, she gritted her teeth, adjusting her grip, while the Dragoon swayed left and right before finally leveling out.
On another Dragoon, Wallace was testing his own skills.
His approach was more aggressive, pushing the craft forward in sudden bursts.
The machine rocked, nearly scraping the workshop wall, before he corrected the angle.
He laughed nervously, muttering, "Alright... not as easy as it looks."
Kai wryly smiled, watching them both.
Their movements were clumsy, but the machines were responsive.
Victor’s modifications had worked... the Dragoons were stable, just waiting for their riders to learn the rhythm.
Minutes passed, and both Mei and Wallace began to improve.
Mei’s Dragoon glided smoothly across the yard, banking in wide curves.
Wallace also managed a sharp turn without losing control...
As expected, his confidence grew with each maneuver.
Victor grinned beside Kai.
"See?
They’ll get the hang of it.
The systems are solid."
Kai nodded.
"Not bad.
It’s rough at first, but once you trust the stabilizers, I guess it feels natural."
Finally, it was his turn.
He climbed into the third Dragoon, settling into the seat.
The handlebars felt firm and the controls felt responsive.
With a tilt forward, the craft surged into the air, pressing him down with sudden force.
’Whoa~’
The wind whipped against his face as he climbed higher.
Kai banked left, then right, testing the stabilizers.
Whoosh~ Whoosh~
The Dragoon obeyed flawlessly, cutting through the air seamlessly.
He skimmed low over the compound, then pulled up into a hover above the walls.
"Responsive," Kai muttered, pushing the craft harder.
He dove, pulled into tight turns, and stopped abruptly mid‐air.
The Dragoon handled every maneuver smoothly, Victor’s rework proving its worth.
’This is an incredible work...
I have to reward him again.’
Victor was a talent he couldn’t lose.
If he needed to bribe him with some of the Superior Gift Packs, he wouldn’t mind it at all.
Minutes passed, and Kai felt the rhythm of the machine...
"I guess having a higher level helped me easily learn how to pilot it." Kai muttered.
Soon, he landed smoothly and dismounted with a satisfied look on his face.
"How was it?" Victor asked.
"It’s stable.
More than I expected.
With three of these, we can move fast..."
Victor nodded.
"So?
What’s the plan?"
He already had an answer in his mind, but he wanted to hear it from Kai.
Kai smiled as he looked toward the horizon.
"It’s time.
We’ll use the Dragoons to reach Cameron.
The Human City might hold the tech we need... and the answers we’ve been waiting for."
Mei and Wallace exchanged excited glances...
The decision was made.
The Codebreakers were no longer bound to three shelters...
Their path to Cameron had just opened.
Just like that, Kai decided to bring a total of five people with him to Cameron.
Although the invitation from Cornelio Aries was for Kai alone, the man had also mentioned that Level 30 Survivors are all welcome in the city...
With that in mind, he chose Mei, Claire, Alfie, Farrah, and Ralph...
Kai would ride with Mei, Claire with Alfie, and Ralph with Farrah on the last modified Dragoon.
Of course, Kai knew that leaving for Cameron couldn’t be rushed.
Even with three Dragoons ready, the shelters had to be secured first.
The twenty‐two newcomers who had arrived days earlier were still settling in.
Kai had already decided they couldn’t all remain in one place.
If they were scattered across the three shelters, even if some had hidden intentions, they wouldn’t be able to cause significant trouble.
"Divide them," Kai ordered during the meeting with the other important members of his shelter.
"Seven to Shelter‐28, eight to Freedom Shelter, and the rest here in New Haven‐45.
That way, we balance the risk and strengthen each base."
Before leaving, Kai assigned the managers...
Victor and Wallace were assigned to oversee New Haven‐45.
Their mechanical expertise and leadership would keep the heart of the Codebreakers strong.
Sera, alongside his Sentinel Atom, would take charge of Haven‐28.
Silas was already producing modified Sentinels there, and Sera’s cautious nature made him the right choice to guard against any sabotage.
Althea and Aurora were tasked with Freedom Shelter.
The crops there had finally begun to flourish, and protecting the food supply was critical.
"That field is our lifeline," Kai reminded them.
"Guard it as if it were the walls themselves."
With the preparations underway, Kai turned his attention to the newcomers.
Among them, three stood out...
Henry, Nadia, and Enzo.
He knew they were also Foreign Survivors, transmigrated into this world, each with skills and talents that could prove invaluable.
’I guess it’s time to complete that Guild Mission...’
Kai found Henry near the training yard, his rifle slung across his back.
The man’s posture was disciplined, and his eyes swept across every corner as though he expected an ambush at any moment.
He looked interesting, but Kai was intrigued upon seeing the man’s eyes...
"Is that an Ocular Replacement Implant?" Kai asked.
Henry froze, stunned by the question.

chapters.title: Chapter 238: Recruitment and Guild Mission Completion
paragraphs: Some time ago, Henry, Nadia, and Enzo stood among the crowd as the modified Dragoons moved across the sky.
The machines flew above the compound, with their thrusters leaving trails of wind...
Henry couldn’t help but feel a rush of excitement after seeing them fly that fast...
"It’s stable and fast... Whoever rebuilt those knows what they’re doing."
Nadia also nodded as she watched the survivors cheer. "They’re incredible. Enzo, can you do that as well?"
Enzo wryly smiled after hearing that. "Mhmm? I can work on their machinery but they’re programmed to attack humans. There’s nothing I can do about that."
Still, after seeing Modified Sentinels, it was no longer surprising to see modified Dragoons. This shelter was already innovating.
"I’d like to get a look at those circuits." He muttered.
The three exchanged glances. They had seen shelters collapse, watched defenses crumble, and endured famine.
But here, in Haven‐45, things were different. The walls are strong, the guards are reliable, and the food supply is nothing to worry about.
Even the machines, once their greatest fear, were under human control.
Still, duty called.
They weren’t living here for free...
Their assigned task was simple but necessary... gather firewood.
Winter was coming, and the signs were clear. It was noticeable since each morning carried a chill, and the nights grew steadily colder.
For now, Henry led the way into the nearby forest with a rifle slung across his back.
He scanned the treeline constantly, just in case they were attacked.
"Stay alert. Even if this area’s been cleared, we don’t take chances."
Nadia followed as she carried her axe... With her current level, gathering wood wasn’t really that tough. Her strength as Level 23 was not something that could be ignored.
Enzo hefted an axe as he found a spot...
Soon, they started chopping through a branch and gathered a bundle of smaller sticks if they couldn’t find larger ones.
Just like that, they worked in silence for a while...
There was only the sound of chopping and gathering of wood...
By the time they returned to the shelter, their arms were stacked with firewood.
As they stepped back through the gates, the sight of the Dragoons resting near Victor’s workshop reminded them once again of the kind of place they had entered.
Then, just as they set down the firewood in the shed near the training yard, Kai approached.
Kai’s gaze focused on Henry’s eyes.
"Is that an Ocular Replacement Implant?" Kai asked.
He recalled the Gene Trader’s catalog from before...

[ Ocular Replacement Implant: A bioengineered eye designed to permanently replace a missing or damaged one. It restores full vision immediately, grants Appraisal Ability, and integrates seamlessly with the body’s nervous system. It guarantees periodic headaches unless the user’s physique is strong enough to negate the strain.
Cost: 10 Survivor Medals ]
Kai had dismissed the item back then.
Well, his own eyes were perfectly fine, and he had already acquired the Fast Appraisal Skill, which made the implant redundant for him.
But for others, it was different. For someone who had lost an eye, the implant wasn’t a luxury to have, it was for survival.
Henry’s expression stiffened when Kai mentioned it.
"You noticed?" he asked.
He had thought the implant blended seamlessly, undetectable to most.
Kai shook his head lightly. "Ahhh... it’s not noticeable at all. I just have my own observation skill. If it were anyone else, they wouldn’t see it unless you activated it."
Henry studied Kai for a moment, then exhaled.
"Yeah... I lost my right eye during an ambush in the Grid Region. A shrapnel tore through my face. Without this implant, I’d be half‐blind. I didn’t have a choice."
Kai nodded. "Well... It’s not really a weakness now. That eye is definitely an asset."
Nadia approached as she heard the exchange.
"Unfortunately, the headaches are real. Although it only happens one or twice a day, it can still be disturbing... I can only give him a pain reliever."
Kai frowned... "The implant’s drawback... periodic headaches. The Gene Trader’s description mentioned it. Unless the user’s physique is strong enough, the nervous system struggles to keep up."
Henry shrugged...
"Guess I’m not strong enough yet. But I’ll manage. Pain is better than blindness."
Kai respected the resolve. He then turned his attention to Nadia.
"You’re a medic, right? Why are you collecting wood? You’re supposed to be helping Elena... or Irene."
Nadia smiled at this. "There’s no one injured anyway... Miss Irene mentioned that I could just help around when there are no patients.
Kai’s lips curved into a faint smile. "That’s more valuable than a rifle. Survivors die faster from untreated wounds than from bullets."
Just like that, Kai made a light conversation with Henry, Nadia, and Enzo, who was a mechanic, and offered to help Victor.
"You can ask Victor about that. If he didn’t want your help, you might be able to help with Silas in Haven-28."
Henry and the others immediately straightened as they heard this...
"Are you sending us to different shelters?"
"Hmm? Do you want to stick together?"
The three then glanced at each other and nodded.
They had survived together in Grid Region, and staying close would be better.
However, Kai’s concern was about their intention... If they were like Terrence or Samantha, then they could be troubling to deal with.
"You’ll only be separated for a month... After that, you can all stick together." Kai explained...
Thankfully, the three of them agreed.
Seeing this, Kai finally revealed his true intention... to invite them to his guild.
[ Invitation Sent: Nadia ]
[ Invitation Sent: Henry ]
[ Invitation Sent: Enzo ]
"What? Really?! You’re inviting us to be part of Codebreakers?!" Henry was excited.
"T-thank you for trusting us, Mr. Kai!" Nadia muttered.
"I will be a useful mechanic. Trust me!" Enzo added.
"Just call me, Kai... We’re similar in age... No, I’m probably younger than the three of you." Kai said as he waved his hand.
Soon, he got the confirmation...
[ Enzo has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Henry has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Nadia has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
As soon as he got this, Kai also received the notification.
[ Guild Mission "Survivor Integration" Completed! ]
[ Guild Reputation +10, Energy Core (C-Grade) +2 ]
"Finally..." Kai smiled as the low-grade mission was finally completed. Now, he was praying that it would be replaced by a mid or high difficulty mission.
Unfortunately, his prayer didn’t work!
[ New Guild Mission has been created! ]
[ Mission 3: Survivor Integration II ]
[ Difficulty: Low
Objective: Recruit a total of 30 members into the Guild.
Reward: Guild Reputation +30, Energy Core (B-Grade) +2 ]
"Seriously? Where am I supposed to find them?"

chapters.title: Chapter 239: The Travel
paragraphs: Kai had no idea when this recruitment would be completed, so for now, he checked the other missions.
Well, the old missions had already rotated out, replaced by new objectives.
[ Mission 1: Fortress Expansion ]
[ Difficulty: Low
Objective: Construct 3 defensive watchtowers around the perimeter of the shelter sector with the highest concentration of Guild Members.
Reward: Guild Reputation +50, Energy Core (C‐Grade) x15, Passive Buff +10% defense to all Guild Members for 48 hours ]
"Mhmm... So that’s why Wallace and the others were digging a while ago. They’re preparing the foundation." Kai muttered.
Well, he wasn’t really micromanaging them, so he wasn’t aware of everyone’s plans.
In any case, he turned his attention to the next one.
[ Mission 2: Salvage Operation ]
Difficulty: Low
Objective: Recover 5 C-Grade Mechanical Units and 10 Weapons from wrecked A.I. Units in the southern ruins.
Reward: Guild Reputation +50, Energy Core (C‐Grade) x15, Beginner Crafting Material Pack x2
Kai couldn’t help but smile after seeing this.
"Finally... something different. Still low-tier, but the rewards are quite decent." Kai muttered.
Meanwhile, the three new members were elated upon seeing the Guild Feature opening up.
"So this is... the Guild System? Missions, rewards, objectives... it’s all real." Henry muttered.
Nadia nodded as she had only learned about this through the World Chat.
"Guild Storage... Guild Reputation... Interesting. So it’s organized like this."
Enzo chuckled as he also started exploring the new window screen.
"There’s also Guild Chat and Guild Missions... this is insane. Communication with everyone also became so easy with this."
Kai watched their reactions calmly. For him, the interface was familiar, but for them it was their first glimpse into what being part of a guild truly meant.
Henry muttered, half to himself, "I will do my best to help with the construction of the towers."
"Good. You need contribution points anyway." Kai muttered.
Nadia nodded quickly. "And the rewards aren’t just for one person. Buffs for everyone, resources for the guild... it makes survival collective. This is nice."
Enzo grinned. "I thought joining a guild was just about sticking together. But this is a whole different level..."
Kai gave a faint smile. It seemed that Enzo wasn’t familiar with how Guild Works in games.
"Yes... This is what guild does... It was basically rewards unity."
The three newcomers exchanged glances, their excitement was clear.
Kai closed the interface. "You’ll get used to it. Missions like these will shape the guild’s strength. And now that you’re part of Codebreakers, you’ll see how far we can go."
Henry clenched his fist. "Yes! We’ll prove ourselves."
"We won’t let you down." Nadia and Enzo added.
Satisfied with their response, Kai finally left. If they have any further questions, they could just use their chat for faster communication.
The next day, Kai stood in the yard while looking at the three modified Dragoons on the ground. Survivors gathered near the gates, watching silently.
At this time, everyone already knew their plan to visit the human city, Cameron.
Then, Mei finally arrived as she adjusted her gloves before she mounted the first Dragoon.
After that, Kai climbed behind her.

Well, Mei insisted on piloting the flying vessel, and Kai didn’t argue. As a matter of fact, he also felt that it would be fine to let her take control since he could protect them in case they were ambushed.
With his various skills, he was confident that he’d be able to protect Mei in case of an emergency.
Just like that, Claire and Alfie took the second, while Ralph and Farrah settled onto the third. Their packs were already secured, including their weapons.
Soon, Victor stepped forward with his hands stained with oil from another long night of work.
He actually made a few adjustments last night to ensure that the modified dragoons would be safe to operate.
"Ahem... The stabilizers are solid. Don’t push them too hard on the first stretch. And remember... Cameron’s north. We’ve seen the Flying Fortress go in that direction before... Be careful."
Kai nodded. He also recalled the floating island or fortress from before. It means that the path leading to the human city was definitely dangerous.
"We’ll be careful. Keep the shelters steady until we return."
Wallace and Irene also stood together, offering quiet smiles. Wallace gave a salute, while Irene was praying for the group.
Kai looked over the crowd one last time. "We’ll bring back what we can. Cameron might hold the answers we need. Until then... protect each other."
The gates creaked open, and the three Dragoons surged forward.
Whoosh~ Whoosh~ Whoosh~
Dust swirled in their wake as the machines lifted higher with its engines humming with Victor’s handiwork.
"Goodbye!" voices called from below.
The survivors waved, the guards raised their rifles in attention, and the newcomers watched with awe as the guild’s leaders vanished into the horizon.
Kai tightened his grip on Mei’s shoulders as the wind rushed past.
The compound shrank behind them, and just like that, Haven‐45 became a speck against the vast wasteland.
Ahead, the northern cliff stretched endlessly... It means that the path to Cameron was long and uncertain.
But Kai’s resolve was firm. With three Dragoons and his chosen team, he didn’t care about the distance...
He had brought enough C-Grade Cores as well to ensure their uninterrupted journey!
We, he traded those cores with the other Survivors using his Infinite Gift Pack.
Soon, the Dragoons cut through the wasteland skies for hours, their engines ran steadily as the team pressed north.
The wind was strong, and the terrain below was shifting from barren plains to jagged ridges.
After nearly five hours of travel, Kai signaled for the group to slow down. Ahead, the ground grew rocky, cliffs were rising unevenly, and the remains of a small shelter came into view.
Mei tilted her Dragoon slightly, squinting. "There’s a settlement down there... but it looks terrible."
Claire frowned.
"Could be abandoned. Or worse, attacked." She said on the radio.
Kai also focused and used his Keen Sense to scan the perimeter... As soon as he did so, he noticed something strange.
"Mhmm?"

The wind was strong, and the terrain below was shifting from barren plains to jagged ridges.
After nearly five hours of travel, Kai signaled for the group to slow down.
Ahead, the ground grew rocky, cliffs were rising unevenly, and the remains of a small shelter came into view.
Mei tilted her Dragoon slightly, squinting.
"There’s a settlement down there... but it looks terrible."
Claire frowned.
"Could be abandoned.
Or worse, attacked." She said on the radio.
Kai also focused and used his Keen Sense to scan the perimeter...
As soon as he did so, he noticed something strange.
"Mhmm?"

chapters.title: Chapter 241: Steady Supply
paragraphs: Kai pressed the activation switch, and the generator’s panel lit up with a faint vibration...
Soon, the vents of the device began pulling in air, condensation forming inside the chamber. Within moments, droplets trickled into the reservoir, gathering into a steady stream.

[ Atmospheric Water Generator (Unique): A portable device capable of extracting moisture directly from the air. Produces clean, drinkable water even in arid environments. Output increases in humid conditions. ]

[ Note: Requires steady power input. Consumes 1 C‐Grade Core to function for approximately 6 hours. Provides a continuous supply of water during operation, with output depending on the surrounding humidity. ]
The survivors gasped as the first drops splashed into a dented tin cup.
"This..."
Steven’s hands trembled as he lifted it, staring at the clear liquid. He took a sip, and his eyes widened.
"It’s... fresh. Real water."
Just like that, many of them, including the handful of children, rushed forward, guided by their mothers... They were holding cracked bowls and chipped jars.
Seeing this pitiful scene, Kai adjusted the nozzle, letting the stream flow steadily into their containers.
Then, while doing so, he looked at the group of Foreign Survivors.
Well, they were recognizable since they were wearing the Survivor Gear Set given by the system.
"As you can see, as long as you feed it a C‐Grade Core, it will run for about six hours," Kai explained.
"During that time, it will keep producing water. Enough for everyone here, if you guard it properly."
The crowd celebrated as soon as they heard this.
They were still hungry, but having water was already a good start. At the very least, one problem was sorted out.
Furthermore, with their products produced from the blue grass, they should be able to trade it for some food from these compassionate Survivors.
Just like that, some of them couldn’t contain their emotions. They started crying while some of them were laughing, with a few others kneeling in relief.
A woman clutched her child, whispering thanks.
An older man also fell to his knees with tears streaming down his face as he cupped water in his hands.
This time, Mei and the others really realized how grateful they were to be part of Kai’s Guild.
If not for the resources Kai could produce through the gift packs, they might also be in a similar situation... lacking food and water, eventually draining them as well.
Mei sighed as she saw the situation... "They’ve probably been rationing drops for weeks."
Claire nodded as she started taking out her packed food from the inventory as well. She just couldn’t bear seeing those children so malnourished.
"Kai... Are you going to sell them food as well? For now, I can give a few of my packs for donation. I want the children to have them."
Kai smiled after seeing this.
"Don’t worry. I’m planning to give them some food as well."

At this time, Steven, one of the Foreign Survivors in this shelter, wiped his mouth after drinking... "This generator... it’s worth more than we imagined. We’ll pay the five Survivor Medals you asked for."
As he said this, he immediately took out five of his medals and gave them to Kai without hesitation.
He had no idea how Kai obtained something like this.
Beside him, Vera and Juno exchanged glances before stepping forward.
Vera held out a small pouch. Inside were several vials filled with a dull blue liquid.

"We don’t have much food left, but we’ve been making potions from the blue grass. These are called Soul Boosters... They help recover Spirit Points and provide healing for minor injuries... they’re crude, but they work. If you’re willing, we’ll trade these for more food."
Apparently, the blue grass around them wasn’t just for decoration. It was the main reason why they had settled in this shelter. Unfortunately, these products do not help with their satiety.

For now, Kai studied the vials calmly... He knew they had no idea about his Infinite Gift Pack system... that he could produce as many Food Gift Packs as he wanted. But revealing that would only weaken his bargaining position.
"Potions, huh?" Kai muttered, picking one up and swirling the liquid inside.
He then used his fast appraisal.
[ Fast Appraisal Activated ]
[ Spirit Point Cost: 10 ]
[ Cooldown: 15 seconds ]
Soon, he got the information that he needed.
"Let’s see what we have here..."
[ You have discovered Soul Booster Potion! ]
[ Grade: Rare Consumable ]

[ Description: A 10mL potion brewed from processed blue soul grass. Restores 30 Spirit Points and accelerates recovery from minor injuries. Crude in refinement, but effective for short‐term survival. ]
[ Note: Single‐use consumable. Recovery effects last for approximately 15 minutes. Overconsumption may cause dizziness or nausea. ]
Kai gently nodded as he read through the appraisal. "Hmm... not bad. It’s rough, but it works. Spirit recovery and minor healing... "
Steven and Vera waited nervously for his judgment.
Kai finally nodded. "Alright. I’ll accept these potions as part of the trade. Survivor Medals and Soul Boosters in exchange for the water generator and the food packs."
Relief washed over the survivors. Vera clutched the pouch tighter, grateful that their crude alchemy had worth.
Even though they didn’t know how much food they would get, they were still happy with this transaction.
After all, they believed that these people wouldn’t scam them.
Soon, Kai learned that the survivors could provide him with a total of 12 Survivor Medals and 32 Soul‐Booster Potions.
With that in mind, Kai decided to be generous.
Twelve Medals were extremely useful for him, after all.
"Alright," Kai said calmly. "I’ll accept the Medals and the potions. In return, I’ll give you food and water packs. But I’ll need a safe room to store everything."
Steven nodded quickly. "There’s one room that wasn’t completely destroyed. It’s secure enough."
Kai followed him to the shelter’s interior. The room was cracked and worn, but the walls still held firm. It was enough.
Just like that, Kai began unloading his supplies. One by one, the packs materialized, filling the room.
He decided to give them, 10 Basic Food Gift Packs, 5 Enhanced Food Gift Packs, 5 Superior Food Gift Packs, 5 Enhanced Water Gift Packs, and finally, 1 Superior Water Gift Pack.
Just like that, the room was overflowing with resources...
However, Kai knew that he couldn’t miss this opportunity...
’I want that steady supply of Soul Boosters...’

chapters.title: Chapter 242: The Talents
paragraphs: From Basic to Superior, the changes of the packs weren’t just the quality of the content, it was also the quantity.
[ Food Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: canned goods, instant noodles, granola bars, tea bags, and mayonnaise. ]
[ Food Gift Pack (Enhanced)
Contents: vacuum‐sealed rations, canned goods, dried fruits and nuts, instant soup packs, coffee sachets, and portable cooking stove with fuel canisters. ]
[ Food Gift Pack (Superior)
Contents: dehydrated meal packs, protein concentrate packs, hydroponic starter kit, fruit juice packs, portable cooking stove with extra fuel canisters. ]
While the Basic ones could feed a person for about two weeks, the Enhanced packs could feed you for a month.
However, for the Superior Gift Pack, the meal packs alone could feed someone for a month. With the hydroponic kit and the juice packs, it would increase even more.
Kai stood in the storage room, and after feeling satisfied, he looked behind him.
The survivors marvel at the piles of food and water packs.
Steven, Vera, and Juno lingered close, clearly waiting for his next words.
At this time, Kai spoke...

"You’ve given me Survivor Medals and Soul Booster Potions. That’s a good start. But I don’t want this to be a one‐time deal. I want consistency. If you can keep producing potions, I’ll make sure you never worry about food or water again."
Vera’s eyes widened. "You mean... a steady exchange? So... we brew potions, and you’ll keep supplying us?"
Kai nodded firmly. "Exactly. But if possible, I want to have something more than trade. I want loyalty... I want you in my Guild."
As soon as he said this, the three froze for a moment, then exchanged glances.
They had already introduced themselves and knew that he was Kai, the Rank 1 Survivor in the leaderboard.
Juno spoke first. "Guild... You mean... the Codebreakers? We’ve seen the name in the leaderboard. You’re the leader, right?"
Kai chuckled and nodded. "Yes. Codebreakers. If you join, you’ll have protection, resources, and a future. So... How many of you here are Foreign Survivors?"
With this question, they immediately recalled that only the Foreign Survivors could actually join a guild.
Steven counted in his mind before he answered. "Only six of us are left... The rest are locals who were already here before the machines rose."

Kai nodded slowly. "Six, huh... Alright... If you join, you’ll be compensated properly for the potions you’re making. I just want a steady supply of Soul Boosters, or if you can make something even better, then that’s perfect."
Vera clutched her pouch nervously. "We can manage... maybe fifteen potions a week, if the blue soul grass keeps growing. It takes time to refine them."

Kai considered this, then spoke decisively. "I can have ten per week... You can save the rest for yourself. Still, I’ll keep supplying food in exchange. If you can increase production later, even better."
Steven’s eyes lit up. "That’s... manageable. And if we’re in your Guild, we won’t have to worry about starving anymore."
Juno added quickly, "We’ll do it. We’ll make as many potions as we can. Just promise us the children won’t go hungry again."
Kai’s expression softened slightly. "As long as you keep your end of the deal, I’ll keep mine. Food will never be a problem for you again."
The three bowed immediately... "We’ll join Codebreakers," Steven declared. "From now on, we’ll brew potions for you. Every week, without fail."
Kai extended his hand, and Steven clasped it firmly. Vera and Juno followed suit...
As their hands met, Kai’s eyes lingered briefly on Vera.
Her short red hair framed her face, and even if she still looked really weak, her features carried a striking beauty.
Anyway, she was the only woman among the Foreign Survivors here, so Kai noted that her presence.
’She’ll stand out in the Guild,’ Kai thought as he had a hard time turning his attention away.
’Not just for her skills, but for her presence.’
In any case, Juno looked young... too young. He seemed to be a teenager, someone who had just graduated from high school.
Nonetheless, the rest of the Foreign Survivors were men.
They lacked Vera’s striking appearance or Juno’s youthful spark, but their willingness to pledge themselves spoke volumes.
Kai finally asked, "How many survivors are here in total?"
Steven answered quickly. "Thirty‐two. That includes the six of us who are Foreign Survivors."
Kai nodded. "Then only the six of you can join Codebreakers..."
At that moment, the system notifications appeared before Kai’s eyes:
[ Invitation Sent: Steven ]
[ Invitation Sent: Vera ]
[ Invitation Sent: Juno ]
[ Invitation Sent... ]
Soon, the confirmations followed:
[ Steven has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Vera has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Juno has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ ... has joined Codebreakers Guild. ]
[ Guild Mission Progress Updated: Survivor Integration II ]
[ Current Members: 21 / 30 ]
As soon as the confirmation was made and they saw the new guild feature, they finally celebrated!
"Codebreakers... Awesome!"
"We did it! We’re going to work hard, Sir Kai!"
Soon, the cheers slowly faded as Kai raised his hand, signaling for silence. His eyes swept over the new members...

"Now that you’re part of Codebreakers," Kai said firmly, "there’s no need for secrets. I need to know your talents. If you’re going to contribute to the Guild, I want to understand what each of you can do."
Steven straightened...

"I’ll start. My talent is Iron Will Combatant. It’s a Superior Grade combat talent. When I fight, my endurance and resistance to pain increase drastically. Even if I’m wounded, I can keep going. It doesn’t make me stronger in terms of raw power, but it lets me fight longer than most."
Kai nodded as he turned his gaze to Vera.

She hesitated for a moment, clutching her pouch, before speaking softly. "My talent is Alchemist. Unfortunately, it’s only a Rare Grade alchemy talent. It’s the reason we’ve been able to make Soul Booster Potions. I can refine herbs and plants into usable tonics. The blue soul grass here responds especially well to my ability. Without me, those potions wouldn’t exist."
’An alchemist... that’s rare among survivors...’Kai mused as he gave a faint smile. "Even if it’s Rare, it’s still amazing."
As he thought that it was the most amazing Talent among the group, Juno finally spoke.
"I have Master-Grade Telekinetic Talent."

chapters.title: Chapter 243: The Talents and the Upgrade Crystal
paragraphs: Kai’s eyes widened as Juno spoke.
’Telekinesis... a Master‐Grade Talent.’
He had seen many talents by now... Pathfinder, Sharpshooter, Mechanic, and even rare crafting talents, but this was different.
"You can control things with your mind or something?" Kai asked.
"That’s right..."
Kai nodded in satisfaction.
’Incredible. If he can truly manipulate objects with his mind, then that’s definitely useful. But how strong is it?’
He wanted to test it, but he also knew they were exhausted.
Hunger and thirst had drained them to the point of collapse.
"Alright," Kai said as he looked at the six foreign Survivors.
"We’ll talk more about your talents later. For now, everyone eats."

The survivors’ eyes lit up as Kai and his Guild members distributed the food packs. Cracked bowls and chipped jars were filled with steaming soup, dried fruits, and ration bars. After weeks of struggling, the shelter smelled of real food.
Children laughed as they sipped juice from the Superior packs, while mothers clutched them tightly with tears streaming down their faces.
As they ate, Juno explained further.
"My Telekinetic Talent automatically gave me the Gene Skill Telekinesis... It’s different from other talents."
Kai paused as he heard this.
"Wait... You have a Gene Skill by default?"
"That’s right. I think Talents like mine had that perk. There are others like me in the World Chat though. I saw some of them talking about it."
"Ah... I don’t regularly check the World Chat. I’m only checking the Chat at night before sleeping. I guess I’ll try to keep updated from now on."
"You should..." Juno said. He was genuinely shocked that Kai wasn’t always updated in the World Chat.
He remembered that when he reached Level 20, he’d always be in the World Chat, carefully considering when to use his limited daily chats.
Well, there’s no internet here after all. There wasn’t really that much to do if the enemies weren’t attacking them and if there was food around.
This time, however, it seemed that he had a lot of work to do.
Anyway, Juno continued to explain.
"I can move objects with Spirit Energy. Small things for now, but with training, I can probably push further. I just need more Skill Points"
Kai gently nodded... "That’s amazing."
"Yes. It drains Spirit Points quickly, but it’s useful. I can lift weapons, block attacks, even throw debris. It’s why I survived this long."
Claire and Mei exchanged glances, clearly impressed. Even Steven looked proud to have Juno among them.
Kai then turned his attention to the other three Foreign Survivors. "What about the rest of you? Tell me your talents."

The first man, a burly figure with calloused hands, spoke. "Mine is Sculptor Talent. It’s... not combat‐related. I can shape stone and wood more easily, refine materials faster. It’s only a Rare Grade, but it helps with shelter repairs."
Kai nodded thoughtfully. "That’s still useful. Crafting and construction are vital for survival."
He didn’t expect to find a sculptor here...
"I hope that if you reach a higher level, your sculptures will have some kind of special effects."
"I was hoping for that too... Have you read about the Legendary Moonlight Sculptor?"
"Nah... Sorry about that," Kai replied, unsure if it was some sort of movie or drama...

In any case, the second foreign survivor, stepped forward. "I have Quick Feet Talent. Superior Grade. It boosts my speed and agility. I can outrun most enemies, dodge attacks, and carry supplies faster. It’s saved me more than once... But it heavily relies on my Stamina and Spirit Points. If I’m hungry, I can’t really run fast even if I have enough Spirit Points."
Kai gave a faint smile. "Got it... You will be well-fed from now on."
The man chuckled at that and hoped that it was true.
Finally, the third survivor, a quiet young man with soot‐stained fingers, spoke hesitantly. "My talent... is Pyromancer."
The word alone made everyone pause.
Claire’s eyes widened, Mei gasped, and even Alfie muttered in disbelief. "Pyromancer?!"
Kai’s brows rose.
’A Pyromancer... if that’s real, it could change everything.’

Seeing their reaction, the young man quickly waved his hand and clarified with an apologetic tone. "It’s only Common Grade. I can’t conjure fireballs or anything like that. I can make sparks, small flames... enough to light the night, cook food, or scare animals. That’s all."
The excitement in the room dimmed slightly.
The survivors had imagined a warrior who could burn through the A.I. Army with blazing fire. Instead, they had someone who could light campfires.
Kai studied him carefully.
’’Even a Common Grade Pyromancer has potential. If it were Rare, Superior, or Master Grade, it would be devastating. But Common... it’s limited. Still, fire is fire. And fire can grow.’
The others looked disappointed, but Kai’s lips curved into a knowing smile.
"You’re underestimating yourselves. Have you heard about the Talent Upgrade Crystal?"
The six new members of the Codebreakers exchanged confused glances. "Talent... Upgrade Crystal?" Steven asked.
"What’s that?"
Kai smiled as he saw their curious faces...

"It’s a rare item. When used, it can raise the grade of a talent. Common can become Uncommon. Uncommon can become Rare. Rare can become Superior... and so on. The higher the grade, the stronger the talent’s effects. For a Pyromancer, that means sparks could become flames... flames could become fireballs... and eventually, infernos."
The survivors stared at him, stunned. Vera clutched her chest and asked once more.
"You mean... talents can evolve?"
Kai nodded. "Yes. It’s not easy to obtain, but it exists. I’ve already used one."
The Pyromancer’s eyes widened, he was now filled with hope! He had thought that he was already stuck as a human stove forever!
"Thank you for letting me know! I will work hard!"
Just like that, the room was suddenly filled with hope.
Even the children sensed the shift in mood and started eating happily...
However, Mei couldn’t help but nudge Kai...
"Hey... I know you mentioned that before. But how did you get that Talent Upgrade Crystal?"

sentences.text: Kai’s eyes widened as Juno spoke.
’Telekinesis... a Master‐Grade Talent.’
He had seen many talents by now...
Pathfinder, Sharpshooter, Mechanic, and even rare crafting talents, but this was different.
"You can control things with your mind or something?" Kai asked.
"That’s right..."
Kai nodded in satisfaction.
’Incredible.
If he can truly manipulate objects with his mind, then that’s definitely useful.
But how strong is it?’
He wanted to test it, but he also knew they were exhausted.
Hunger and thirst had drained them to the point of collapse.
"Alright," Kai said as he looked at the six foreign Survivors.
"We’ll talk more about your talents later.
For now, everyone eats."
The survivors’ eyes lit up as Kai and his Guild members distributed the food packs.
Cracked bowls and chipped jars were filled with steaming soup, dried fruits, and ration bars.
After weeks of struggling, the shelter smelled of real food.
Children laughed as they sipped juice from the Superior packs, while mothers clutched them tightly with tears streaming down their faces.
As they ate, Juno explained further.
"My Telekinetic Talent automatically gave me the Gene Skill Telekinesis...
It’s different from other talents."
Kai paused as he heard this.
"Wait...
You have a Gene Skill by default?"
"That’s right.
I think Talents like mine had that perk.
There are others like me in the World Chat though.
I saw some of them talking about it."
I don’t regularly check the World Chat.
I’m only checking the Chat at night before sleeping.
I guess I’ll try to keep updated from now on."
"You should..." Juno said.
He was genuinely shocked that Kai wasn’t always updated in the World Chat.
He remembered that when he reached Level 20, he’d always be in the World Chat, carefully considering when to use his limited daily chats.
Well, there’s no internet here after all.
There wasn’t really that much to do if the enemies weren’t attacking them and if there was food around.
This time, however, it seemed that he had a lot of work to do.
Anyway, Juno continued to explain.
"I can move objects with Spirit Energy.
Small things for now, but with training, I can probably push further.
I just need more Skill Points"
Kai gently nodded...
"That’s amazing."
"Yes.
It drains Spirit Points quickly, but it’s useful.
I can lift weapons, block attacks, even throw debris.
It’s why I survived this long."
Claire and Mei exchanged glances, clearly impressed.
Even Steven looked proud to have Juno among them.

"What about the rest of you?
Tell me your talents."

It’s... not combat‐related.
I can shape stone and wood more easily, refine materials faster.
It’s only a Rare Grade, but it helps with shelter repairs."
Kai nodded thoughtfully.
"That’s still useful.
Crafting and construction are vital for survival."
He didn’t expect to find a sculptor here...
"I hope that if you reach a higher level, your sculptures will have some kind of special effects."
"I was hoping for that too...
Have you read about the Legendary Moonlight Sculptor?"
"Nah...
Sorry about that," Kai replied, unsure if it was some sort of movie or drama...

Superior Grade.
It boosts my speed and agility.
I can outrun most enemies, dodge attacks, and carry supplies faster.
It’s saved me more than once...
But it heavily relies on my Stamina and Spirit Points.
If I’m hungry, I can’t really run fast even if I have enough Spirit Points."
Kai gave a faint smile.
"Got it...
You will be well-fed from now on."

chapters.title: Chapter 244: The Status Crystal
paragraphs: "Mhm... right, you only got fragments," Kai muttered, recalling that Claire had mentioned it to him earlier.
Apparently, they had only managed to obtain a fragment, while Kai had been rewarded with a complete Talent Upgrade Crystal after securing Rank 1 on the Leaderboard during the first cycle.
Then, the next upgrade crystal came after becoming the first Guild Leader.
After sharing that with Mei, she could only accept that it would be really difficult to upgrade a Talent.
Right now, she only had 2 Fragments... If her only way of getting one was staying within the Top 20 Survivors, it would take her three more months to achieve that.
"I hope there’s another method to get them." She muttered.

"I’ll let you know if I find something related. Maybe the Reputation Store will sell one someday." Kai said as he believed that it was possible, considering the fact that the store was selling system-related items like the Guild Expansion Token.
After Kai explained the Talent Upgrade Crystal’s existence, he soon realized that it was getting late.
"We’ll stay here tonight. Tomorrow, we’ll continue our journey to Cameron City. But for now, this shelter needs rebuilding."
The six of them, Kai, Mei, Alfie, Claire, Farrah, and Ralph, immediately set to work.

Since this place was basically part of their Guild already, they weren’t just going to leave this place broken. They felt that they had a responsibility to strengthen the places under their protection.
Kai walked outside with Wallace and the others, surveying the cracked walls and makeshift tents.
The locals, twenty‐six in total, had all just finished satisfying their hunger. They regained some energy, but they still needed some rest.
However, Kai and his team couldn’t stay here for long, so they must work immediately. Soon, he raised his voice so everyone could hear.
"From today onward, Codebreakers will take care of this shelter. You’ll have food, water, and protection. But we’ll need your cooperation to rebuild this place..."
Of course, the announcement was still me with cheers and relieved murmurs.
Children clapped, while the adults nodded eagerly.
Kai then activated his Infinite Gift Pack system and withdrew several Gift Packs.
[ Shelter Gift Pack (Enhanced)
Contents: field tent, insulated sleeping bag, heavy‐duty flashlight, thermal blanket, heavy‐duty raincoat. ]
[ Shelter Gift Pack (Superior)
Contents: modular survival pod, weatherproof clothing set, perimeter alarm system set, portable air filtration device, calming incense set, and sleeping bag. ]
He opened five Enhanced Shelter Gift Packs and two Superior Shelter Gift Packs. Immediately, crates materialized, filled with neatly packed supplies.
The locals gasped in amazement.
Field tents were unfolded and raised, giving families proper shelter for the first time in a while.

As soon as it was built, children ran inside, laughing as they touched the insulated sleeping bags. Heavy‐duty flashlights were distributed. Then, thermal blankets and raincoats were handed out, ensuring protection against the elements.
After all, from a single Enhanced Pack, they could already have three flashlights and three raincoats.
But the greatest excitement came when Kai revealed the two Superior Gift Packs. The modular survival pods were unlike anything the locals had ever seen. Compact crates unfolded into sturdy frames.
Soon, they built the pods...
The panels clicked into place, and in just a few minutes, the pods were assembled step by step... These pods may not be big, but they would provide secure, insulated living quarters.

After that, the portable air filtration devices hummed softly, providing them with clean air. Weatherproof clothing sets were also distributed, replacing the ragged garments the survivors had worn for months.
Then, the perimeter alarm systems were carefully installed. As soon as they learned what it could do, it reassured everyone that danger would be detected before it struck!
Finally, the calming incense was lit near the pods, and its faint aroma was already easing the tension in the air. Just like that, the shelter felt like a place of peace...
Vera then approached Kai hesitantly. "Sir... Leader Kai... if I wanted more of these Gift Packs... could I pay with potions or Survivor Medals? Or maybe some other ways?"
As she said the last part, Kai noticed that she had somehow fixed her hair.
"Ahem..."
Anyway, Kai studied her carefully before answering. "I spend Survivor Medals to obtain these. If you want extra Gift Packs, I’ll only accept Survivor Medals. And this must remain secret."
Vera’s eyes widened, then she nodded quickly. "I promise. I’ll keep it secret. I’ll collect Survivor Medals, and once I have enough, I’ll let you know."
Kai gave a faint smile. "Good..."
Soon, the night settled over the shelter, as they stayed with the tents...
They then had some late snacks before they wrapped themselves in thermal blankets, and slept soundly.
Tomorrow, they will be traveling to Cameron City!
The next morning, before leaving the shelter that Vera and the others had begun callingBlue Grass Shelter, Kai decided to make one final check.
He retrieved the Status Crystal, its faint glow pulsing as he poured Spirit Energy into it.

[ Status Crystal: A rare crystal that reveals the complete status of the person who touches it. When activated, it displays their name, title, level, skills, and stats for exactly 10 seconds before fading.
Cooldown: 30 seconds
Charge: 50 ]
Kai held the crystal up for everyone to see what must be done.
The survivors lined up nervously. One by one, they placed their hands on the crystal.
The first was a middle‐aged man.
[ Name: Leron ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 5 ]
[ Spirit: 40 / 40 ]
[ Physique Rating: E ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Hardy Constitution Lv0 ]
[ Hardy Constitution (Level 0): Grants minor resistance to fatigue and illness. Slightly improves recovery rate when resting. ]
Kai nodded. It was quite a good skill but not enough to take note of.
Next was a young woman.
[ Name: Maris ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 5 ]
[ Health: 85 / 115 ]
[ Spirit: 70 / 70 ]
[ Physique Rating: E‐ ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Forager’s Instinct Lv0 ]
[ Forager’s Instinct (Level 0): Improves ability to identify edible plants and safe water sources. Slightly increases efficiency when gathering food. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 245: The Last Gifts and the Journey to Cameron
paragraphs: "Incredible... So we really have status like the Foreign Survivors."
"This is amazing... Our name, health, and other stats are listed. It’s something I didn’t even know I had."
"Status Crystal... This thing must be expensive."
"I wonder if I have a Title. Wait... How do we even get one?"
"This looked so mystical."
"How is that thing working? Wait... His health is low... You need to eat more!"
The local survivors, including Vera and others, had never seen the status crystal. They just followed Kai’s instructions, and as soon as they saw the
As expected, the Level 5 Survivors had one Gene Skill at the very least. They must’ve used Gene Enhancement Serums to reach this level, which shouldn’t be that surprising anymore.
Just like that, Kai continued to check the others with the Status Crystal.
The next was a thin man with weary eyes. He still looked malnourished at his point but he was able to smile at him.
[ Name: Randel ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 5 ]
[ Health: 70 / 130 ]
[ Spirit: 55 / 55 ]
[ Physique Rating: E ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Stone Endurance Lv0 ]
[ Stone Endurance (Level 0): Slightly increases resistance to fatigue when working with heavy loads. Provides minor tolerance against blunt force impacts. ]
Kai nodded faintly. "Useful for labor, but not combat."
Just like that, several more people got checked, and most of them were level 3 and level 4 individuals. It means that they do not have any Gene Skills whatsoever.
As for the children, it was quite expected, but they were all just level one with average Health and Spirit Points.
Then, as Kai thought that there weren’t any more skilled individuals, another woman stepped forward with her hands trembling as she touched the crystal.
[ Name: Emiru ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 5 ]
[ Health: 50 / 110 ]
[ Spirit: 50 / 50 ]
[ Physique Rating: E‐ ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Herbal Sense Lv0 ]
[ Herbal Sense (Level 0): Improves ability to identify medicinal plants. Slightly increases efficiency when preparing basic remedies. ]
"Herbal Sense, huh..." Kai gently nodded as he saw this. He could only guess that she was Vera’s assistant in making those booster potions. Well, it shouldn’t be surprising to have a helper or two.
"Very well..."
He could only take note of her as she would certainly be helpful, considering how his shelters were growing.
In any case, there were a few more locals, but once again, they were just Level 1 to Level 4 individuals with no Gene Skills whatsoever.
After the Status Checking session...
He was ready to leave... However, he noticed that they actually lacked the firepower to protect themselves against a serious raid.
Well, he didn’t want this shelter to be in shambles once he returned to get the potions.

Since food was solved for at least a month if they ration carefully, and water was already somewhat resolved thanks to the atmospheric water generators, he might as well fix the problem with their firepower.
They needed weapons!
’If we leave them like this, this shelter could be overrun and filled with corpses before we return.’
He turned to Vera and Steven.
"I can give you some weapons. You can pay for them later."
The two exchanged surprised glances. "Weapons?" Steven asked.

Kai nodded. "I can see that right now, you’re relying on crossbows, spears, and slingshots. And I noticed you have rifles taken from Sentinels, but you don’t have enough ammunition. And those five plasma rifles... they only have two or three shots left each. That’s not enough."
The survivors listened intently and nodded.
Kai raised his hand, activating his Infinite Gift Pack system once more.
[ Weapon Gift Pack (Enhanced)
Contents: semi‐automatic handgun with spare magazines, axe, combat knife, extra ammunition, tactical holster. ]
He opened five Enhanced Weapon Gift Packs.
Just like that, crates appeared, each containing a Beretta M9 semi‐automatic handgun with spare magazines and extra ammunition. Alongside them were axes, combat knives, and tactical holsters.
The survivors gasped as the weapons were distributed. The handguns looked so precious!
They were far superior to their crude slingshots and worn spears. The axes replaced their old, chipped blades, while the combat knives gave them reliable close‐combat options.
Kai wasn’t finished. He then withdrew two Superior Weapon Gift Packs.
[ Weapon Gift Pack (Superior)
Contents: carbine rifle with spare magazines, shotgun with shell packs, spear, combat knife, protective vest, grenade launcher with smoke and fragmentation rounds, and extra ammunition crates. ]

Two large crates materialized, and when opened, the locals nearly shouted in excitement. Carbine rifles with spare magazines, shotguns with shell packs, and protective vests were handed out. The grenade launchers, complete with smoke and fragmentation rounds, were carefully explained by Kai himself.
The extra ammunition crates were stacked neatly, ensuring that the rifles and shotguns wouldn’t run dry anytime soon.
Then, Kai decided to give their first Stealth Gift Pack.
[ Stealth Gift Pack (Superior)
Contents: advanced camouflage gear, thermal detection goggles, portable disruptor field unit, flashbang grenades, decoy emitter device, and sensor‐disrupting smoke grenades ]
This way, they would be aware of how awesome it was and they’d think of purchasing these as well.
The atmosphere shifted instantly.
The survivors held the weapons with trembling hands as if they were afraid to damage them...
Vera soon clutched her new handgun... "With these... we can actually fight back."
Steven strapped on a protective vest immediately and laughed. "Thank you, Guild Leader! We will be paying for these! I promise! We also won’t let this shelter fall. Not anymore."
Kai looked over them all, satisfied. Now they have a chance. If raiders or Sentinels come, they’ll be able to fight back at the very least.
With the shelter secured, Kai and his team prepared to leave.
Soon, the Dragoons roared to life with their engines echoing across the Blue Grass Shelter.
The locals gathered at the entrance, waving and cheering.
"Thank you, Codebreakers!"
"Safe travels!"
With that, the six of them... Kai, Mei, Alfie, Claire, Farrah, and Ralph, drove their Dragoons out of the Blue Grass Shelter, heading toward Cameron City!

The axes replaced their old, chipped blades, while the combat knives gave them reliable close‐combat options.
Kai wasn’t finished.
He then withdrew two Superior Weapon Gift Packs.
[ Weapon Gift Pack (Superior)
Contents: carbine rifle with spare magazines, shotgun with shell packs, spear, combat knife, protective vest, grenade launcher with smoke and fragmentation rounds, and extra ammunition crates. ]
Two large crates materialized, and when opened, the locals nearly shouted in excitement.
Carbine rifles with spare magazines, shotguns with shell packs, and protective vests were handed out.
The grenade launchers, complete with smoke and fragmentation rounds, were carefully explained by Kai himself.
The extra ammunition crates were stacked neatly, ensuring that the rifles and shotguns wouldn’t run dry anytime soon.
Then, Kai decided to give their first Stealth Gift Pack.
[ Stealth Gift Pack (Superior)
Contents: advanced camouflage gear, thermal detection goggles, portable disruptor field unit, flashbang grenades, decoy emitter device, and sensor‐disrupting smoke grenades ]
This way, they would be aware of how awesome it was and they’d think of purchasing these as well.
The atmosphere shifted instantly.
The survivors held the weapons with trembling hands as if they were afraid to damage them...
Vera soon clutched her new handgun...
"With these... we can actually fight back."
Steven strapped on a protective vest immediately and laughed.
"Thank you, Guild Leader!
We will be paying for these!
I promise!
We also won’t let this shelter fall.
Not anymore."
Kai looked over them all, satisfied.
Now they have a chance.
If raiders or Sentinels come, they’ll be able to fight back at the very least.
With the shelter secured, Kai and his team prepared to leave.
Soon, the Dragoons roared to life with their engines echoing across the Blue Grass Shelter.
The locals gathered at the entrance, waving and cheering.
"Thank you, Codebreakers!"
"Safe travels!"
With that, the six of them...
Kai, Mei, Alfie, Claire, Farrah, and Ralph, drove their Dragoons out of the Blue Grass Shelter, heading toward Cameron City!

chapters.title: Chapter 247: The Beast Machines and the Defenders
paragraphs: The confirmation of their status had barely finished when the alarm thundered across the walls. Sirens rang out, followed by red lights coming on... Just like that, the guards instantly shifted into combat readiness.
Kai turned around, and what he saw made his chest tighten. They were beast-like machines!
"What in the zoid is this?" Ralph muttered as he saw it.
"What do you mean?" Claire asked.
"Forget about it." Ralph waved his hand as he dismissed Claire’s question.
Right now, they have to focus on hiding!
The wolf‐like machines were bristling with weapons. They were charging toward the city in coordinated packs.
But then, the city answered.
From the walls, a storm of firepower came!
"Whoa~" Kai gasped at the sight of Cameron City’s defense.
"This is it... A real fortress against the A.I. Apocalypse." Mei muttered. This was something she really wanted to see!
A full-blown defensive artillery against the mechanical soldiers of the Aria!
Dozens of mounted cannons opened up, unleashing streams of heavy rounds that struck into the advancing mechanical beasts!
Laser batteries tracked targets perfectly, slicing across the battlefield in straight beams that scorched armor and severed limbs.
It didn’t end there, missile pods fired in rapid succession with their trails streaking through the sky before detonating in thunderous bursts among the enemy ranks.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The sound was deafening... A relentless barrage of gunfire, explosions, and shrieking metal followed!
The wolf‐machines were immediately suppressed under the assault...
Kai saw how their armor was easily dented and cracked with some of them collapsing on the ground as their legs were blown apart.
Kai and his team stood frozen at the checkpoint, watching in awe.
Mei’s eyes widened. "That’s... overwhelming. Can’t we all just live here?"
Claire also had the same thoughts. "It must be super expensive to live in this place, Mei. There’s no way it will be free."
Ralph, on the other hand, couldn’t take his eyes away from the mechanical beasts...
"So incredible... They’re dismantling them before they even reach the walls."
"It’s like the city itself is a fortress." Alfie muttered.

The barrage continued, but Kai noticed something... the defenders weren’t firing endlessly. After a few minutes of concentrated fire, the cannons slowed, the missile pods ceased, and the lasers dimmed.
It seemed that they had run out of bullets, or at the very least, they were saving them.
Nonetheless, the beasts had already weakened as their formations were disrupted by the suppression. However, many still crawled forward. They were damaged yet still dangerous.
But then, the second wave of defense.
"W-what?!" Claire’s eyes widened.
"L-look at those! Are you seeing this?" Alfie gasped as he saw something too cool!
From the battlements, figures leapt down!
They were humans clad in rugged exosuits...
Of course, exosuits didn’t look expensive or lustrous. They were used in numerous battle operations. Nonetheless, despite being scarred and dented from countless battles, they looked so reliable!
The armor plating was thick and patched in places with improvised repairs.
As they landed on the ground, their hydraulic limbs hissed as they absorbed the impact...
Soon, Kai and the others heard the guards and other people cheer!
"Ohhh! They’re here!"
"Finally! Hurry, take out your cameras!"
"The Iron Phalanx is here!"
"Haha! Destroy them all!"
Kai and the others remained silent as they saw the regiment called Iron Phalanx come down to end the enemies.
Each of them carried bladed weapons, but they were also equipped with heavy rifles with scratched barrels...
Then, Kai suspected that they were also carrying energy blades aside from the compact launchers strapped to their backs...
"Iron Phalanx, huh..." Kai muttered as he watched the exosuit soldiers move in to intercept the remaining beast-like machines.
It seemed that they were some sort of celebrities, but he could understand why. They all just look so incredible.
As a matter of fact, he also wanted such an exosuit...
Just like that, he watched them charge directly into the weakened beast‐class machines. One slammed into a wolf‐construct, driving its blade through the machine’s neck joint.
Another vaulted over a crippled unit, firing a burst of rounds into its exposed core.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Teams coordinated seamlessly, dismantling the beasts piece by piece.
’I guess they’re saving ammunition by finishing the fight up close...’Kai mused.
"They fight like they’ve done this a hundred times before." Farrah whispered as she realized that this human city wasn’t that completely safe from the A.I. Army.
Ralph, on the other hand, felt so excited.
"Exosuits... so that’s how Cameron City holds against the A.I. Army."
It would definitely be a tough battle if the Beast Machines were in full strength. However, with so much damage done to them, the exosuit soldiers were immediately at an advantage.
They dodged faster, countered, and struck their weak points...
Kai could tell that they had done this hundreds of times.
Still, the Beasts weren’t going to go down without a real fight...
Explosions flared as grenades and missiles were launched.
Unfortunately, they couldn’t watch more of it.
Kai and his team could only look at the closing gates, blocking their view.
The defenders outside continued their battle, but the newcomers were ushered inside quickly. Guards shouted, "Move! Get in before the gates shut!"
Reluctantly, Kai turned away from the fight. He wanted to see it through, but survival came first. The massive gates slammed shut behind them, cutting off the view of the battlefield.
Inside, the atmosphere shifted. The checkpoint guards immediately demanded payment.
"Entry fee. One C‐Grade Core per person."
Kai didn’t hesitate. He and his companions each handed over a C‐Grade Core.
The guards inspected them, then nodded. "Accepted."
In return, they were given small metallic tokens, etched with the city’s insignia.
"Visitor’s tokens. Keep them visible. They’ll mark you as authorized guests."
Kai turned the token in his hand, and he didn’t find anything new about it. It was just a token made of brass.
’So this is Cameron City... even entry comes at a price.’
As Kai turned his attention to the city in front of him, he was soon approached by a guard...
"You’re the one with an invitation token? Can you show it to me again?"

chapters.title: Chapter 248: The Cameron City and the Pod
paragraphs: Kai looked at the guard and confirmed that he was one of those who had handled the Status Crystal a while ago.
After a moment of thought, he reached into his pouch and revealed the Invitation Token. The guard took it carefully...
For a moment, his eyes squinted as he examined the etched markings. Soon, the man’s expression shifted from recognition to caution.
’Mhmm? Is this token special?’Kai mused.
Then, he heard the guard whisper.
"This... this comes from the Aries Faction."
As Kai was processing those words, the guard quickly returned the token to him.
Without another word, he nodded once and stepped back, leaving in a hurry.
Kai blinked, confused. He had no idea what the guard meant. However, he soon recalled Cornelio’s reminder.
’Ahhh... Right. Aries Faction.’
He recalled the existence of Factions within the city! For now, he would be considered a guest of the Aries Faction and it shouldn’t be a bad thing for him.
Regardless, the checkpoint cleared, and Kai’s team was finally allowed into the city proper.
The first area they entered was utilitarian. He could see rows of barracks and military compounds lining the streets... Soon, soldiers and a couple of exosuit operators were moving around.

It was understandable. After all, they were near the gates, so defensive emplacements were scattered throughout... Kai and the others saw mounted turrets and reinforced bunkers positioned strategically.
The air around this area smelled faintly of oil and gunpowder. It was surely a reminder that Cameron City lived under constant threat.
"It feels like the whole entrance is built for war." Alfie muttered.
Ralph nodded. "Makes sense. If the A.I. Army attack this often, the gates have to be the strongest point."
As they walked further in, the scenery began to change.
The military zone gave way to townhouses and mixed‐use buildings, their ground floors converted into shops and stores.
The streets were wide enough for two vehicles to pass side by side, though now they were crowded with people. There were survivors, merchants, and soldiers alike.
Kai’s eyes scanned the bustling scene.
Vendors had set up stalls along the sidewalks, with their voices rising above the crowd as they advertised their goods.
"Fresh homemade sausages! Coconut juice and sweet products get them here!"
"Machine parts, cores, and repair kits!"
"Gene Stimulants and medical supplies!"
"Sword and Gun maintenance! Come!"
It didn’t end there, as the variety was staggering.
Some stalls sold food like dried meats, preserved fruits, and steaming bowls of stew. Others displayed salvaged machine components, glowing cores, and improvised weapons.
A few even offered luxuries like expensive cloth, trinkets, and handmade jewelry, proof that life here wasn’t only about survival.
Alfie grinned. "It’s like a marketplace right outside the gates."
Farrah observed quietly. "They’re smart. With so many people coming in, vendors set up shop where traffic is highest."
Ralph chuckled. "Look at that guy... selling fried bread packs for C-Grade Cores or equal value. So expensive."
Kai couldn’t help but feel impressed.
’This city is interesting.’
The streets were filled with activity... Despite the battle outside, it didn’t stop the chatter, bargaining, and laughter.
The echoes of battle still rumbled faintly beyond the walls, but it was as if they knew that the shelter’s walls wouldn’t collapse at all.
It was definitely their way of showing their faith in the organization protecting the city.
For a moment, Kai and his team absorbed the scene in front of them.
They watched children moved between stalls, clutching small toys made of scrap metal.
They saw soldiers looking around to stop any troublemakers, while some of them were eating quick meals before returning to duty.
Merchants also haggled loudly, as if that would help with the negotiation...
"Amazing... but it’s a pity," Claire muttered. "Everything here is so expensive. We barely have enough C‐Grade Cores, yet in this city they’re treated like everyday currency."

Kai noticed it too. He could only assume it was because Cameron City was strong enough to make such resources commonplace. Out here, C‐Grade A.I. soldiers were considered dangerous foes... but inside these walls, their cores were nothing more than basic trade goods.

As they moved deeper into Cameron City, the team realized the scale of what they had entered. It wasn’t just a fortress... it was a living, breathing community that had carved out a semblance of civilization amidst the chaos.
"Alright! Let’s start looking around!"
"Let’s stick for now. We don’t know what to expect here."
Just like that, Kai and his team ignored most of the stalls as they moved deeper into the city. Food, weapons, and gear were plentiful, but none of it caught their interest.
Kai already had unlimited rations, weapons, and survival equipment.
What they lacked were simple comforts like clothes for sleeping, softer fabrics, things that weren’t designed for combat. But those weren’t urgent, not compared to the essentials they already had.
As they walked past another row of shops, Mei suddenly slowed down.
Her eyes widened as she pointed toward one of the larger buildings.
"Is that... wait... a VR pod?" she asked, her voice filled with disbelief.
He couldn’t understand why it was being sold here.
The others also turned confused.
Through the glass windows of the building, they saw posters plastered across the walls advertising immersive experiences.
And there, displayed prominently, was a capsule‐like machine! It was unmistakably a VR pod.
"What the heck?" Alfie muttered, stepping closer to get a better look.
Claire frowned. "Mhmm? Why is a VR pod being sold like a hot commodity here? There are even different colors."
Farrah’s eyes scanned the poster, and her voice trembled. "Wait... T‐that’s worth one hundred B‐Grade Cores?!"
The group fell silent, stunned.
Kai stared at the pod...
’AVR pod... here, in Cameron City?’
Considering the advancement of technology, it wasn’t really surprising to see a VR pod. However, in this A.I. Apocalypse setting, he couldn’t help but consider this too dangerous.
Even if it could still be used, he never expected to find one openly displayed in a marketplace.

Ralph scratched his head. "Is this their way to escape reality or something? Or maybe they’re using this VR World for something else. Look, they’re selling VR pods for B‐Grade Cores like it’s some luxury item."
Then, it finally clicked...
Kai froze as he recalled the item being sold in his Reputation Store!
"I knew it, I have to buy that thing..."
